findings.detail: HarnessSdkJsonRpcServer.sessions 只在 performShutdown 清空，getOrCreateSession 创建的 agent 从不 dispose；协议 HarnessSdkRequestMap 只有 initialize/session/prompt/shutdown，没有 session 关闭方法。而两个 SDK 的高层 API 在不传 sessionId 时每次 run() 都铸造新 uuid（api.ts:89 `session-${randomUUID()}`、api.py:135 `f"session-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"`）。长驻的 RelayHarness 每 run 一次就在 runtime 进程里永久多一个 agent+session（含持久化句柄与内存），且这些 per-run 会话的 session log 也持续累积。这是"队列有界"原则漏掉的对象生命周期界。
findings.suggested_fix: 在协议上加 session/close（或 session/dispose）请求，服务端实现为 dispose 对应 agent 并从 sessions 移除；短期可先在 server 侧按 idle 后的 TTL/LRU 淘汰 SDK 创建的 agent，并在两个 SDK 的 run() 结束后复用同一 session 或显式关闭。同步更新 packages/sdk/protocol/src/types.ts、两 SDK expected-output（examples/jsonrpc-agent/tests/snapshots/ 与 scripts/snapshots/python-sdk-single-exe/advanced/）。
findings.title: SDK runtime 会话无回收：每次 run() 泄漏一个 agent，直到 shutdown

findings.detail: `if self._proc is not None: return` 在 self._lock 之外，`self._proc = subprocess.Popen(...)` 也在锁外；锁内只清了 session_parents 和 failure 标记。两个线程同时调用 start()（或并发调用 RelayHarness.run 触发的隐式 start）会各 spawn 一个 runtime 子进程，其中一个的 _proc 被覆盖，其 reader/stderr 线程仍在读一个孤儿进程，直到进程退出才失败——资源泄漏且通知被吞。TS 侧 start() 在单线程事件循环里天然安全，这是 Python 独有的生命周期竞态，违反 repo 的 defensive-patterns 意图。
findings.suggested_fix: 把 spawn 整体放进 self._lock 内（锁内先复查 _proc is None 再 Popen 并启动线程），或将 _proc 的写入也纳入锁；在 python/sdk/tests/test_client.py 增加并发 start() 只产生一个子进程的断言。
findings.title: Python HarnessClient.start() 存在双重 spawn 竞态（检查与赋值都在锁外）

findings.detail: TS HarnessClient.close() → performClose 在 `child === undefined` 时直接 return，不执行 failSubscriptions；而 subscribe() 只在 closeTask/exitCode/spawnError 已存在时才 born-failed。于是 `new HarnessClient(o); const sub = client.subscribe(); await client.close(); await sub.next()` 永不 resolve。Python 同构：close() 在 `proc is None` 时早退，不调用 _fail_waiters，NotificationSubscription.next() 每 50ms 空转永远不抛。契约说"after close, rejects immediately"，该路径违背契约。
findings.suggested_fix: TS：performClose 开头无条件 `this.failSubscriptions(this.closedError('Relay Harness runtime closed'))`；Python：close() 把 `self._proc = None` 与 `_fail_waiters(...)` 提到早退之前（或 proc 为 None 时也 fail waiters）。在 packages/sdk/client/tests/sdk-client.spec.ts 与 python/sdk/tests/test_client.py 各补一条 close-without-start 场景。
findings.title: start 之前创建的订阅在 close() 后永远挂起（TS 永久 pending，Python 死循环轮询）

findings.detail: TS initialize() 强制 `serverInfo.name`/`version` 为字符串，否则抛 SdkProtocolError（protocol violation 显式化）；Python 的 `InitializeResponse.serverInfo: ServerInfo | None = None` 且 ServerInfo 两个字段都可 None，pydantic 会对 `{}` 甚至 `null` 静默通过。同一个不守协议的 runtime 在 TS 下响亮失败、在 Python 下返回 name=None 继续运行，违反两 SDK 行为对齐的 repo 约定（AGENTS.md: Both SDKs project the loop），也属于 wire 边界校验缺口。
findings.suggested_fix: Python 的 InitializeResponse 改为必填并在客户端校验 name/version 为非空字符串，失败时抛 SdkProtocolError（errors.py 已有该类型），与 TS 消息对齐；test_client.py 补一条 malformed initialize result 断言（TS 侧已有对应用例 sdk-client.spec.ts:228）。
findings.title: initialize 协议校验不对齐：Python 接受缺失/残缺的 serverInfo，TS 抛 SdkProtocolError

findings.detail: client.ts:7 声明 Python HarnessClient 是 design twin，但投影面已漂移：(1) Python RunResult 暴露 finish_reason 并在最后一个 turn/end 缺 string reason.kind 时抛 SdkProtocolError（api.py:245-262），TS RunResult 无 finishReason、不读 turn/end；(2) Python final_response 在 data.message 缺失时回退读 data.content（api.py:233 content_owner 回退），TS 只读 data.message.content；(3) TS 快照 result.expected.json 只有 sessionId/finalResponse，Python 快照含 events/notifications/session_root，两套 expected-output 记录的投影字段不同，SessionEventMap 变更时无法用同一标准对齐。
findings.suggested_fix: 定一个方向（建议 TS 补 finishReason + 与 Python 相同的 data.content 回退，或 Python 删掉超集），一处实现一处引用；同时统一两套快照的 result 字段集。改 agent-loop 可见面需同 PR 更新 examples/jsonrpc-agent/tests/snapshots/ 与 scripts/snapshots/python-sdk-single-exe/。
findings.title: RunResult 投影不对称：Python 有 finish_reason 且校验 turn/end，TS 完全没有；final_response 读取路径也不一致

findings.detail: 对同一个坏 runtime：TS run() 在 collect 里调用 validatedSessionEvent，非 dict envelope 或 assistant/message 内容畸形直接抛 SdkProtocolError（注释明确写了这是 wire-boundary 校验）；Python collect 用 `if isinstance(event, dict)` 静默跳过，final_response 对缺 message/content 的 assistant 事件 `continue`。结果 Python 会返回 final_response='' 的"成功" RunResult，错误被吞，违反 repo 的错误传播期望（不吞边界错误），也使 parity 断言不可能成立。
findings.suggested_fix: Python 在 collect 路径加与 TS 等价的校验（envelope 必须是含字符串 type 的 dict；assistant/message 的 content 必须是 block 列表），失败抛 SdkProtocolError；在 python/sdk/tests/test_client.py 补对应的 malformed-event 用例（镜像 sdk-client.spec.ts:503-519）。
findings.title: 畸形 session.event 的错误传播相反：TS 抛 SdkProtocolError，Python 静默丢弃

findings.detail: `private model = 'deepseek-official'` 与 provider 默认值相同，几乎肯定是 `deepseek-v4-flash` 的笔误（两个 SDK 客户端默认均为 'deepseek-v4-flash'）。handleRequest 对 prompt 不检查是否已完成 initialize：在 initialize 之前 session/prompt 会用 provider='deepseek-official' + model='deepseek-official' 创建 agent——错误模型名直到首次模型请求才失败，不符合 "Misconfiguration fails loud ... at the earliest resolvable point"。
findings.suggested_fix: 默认 model 改为 'deepseek-v4-flash'，并在 getOrCreateSession（或 prompt）对未 initialize 的调用直接抛错（fail loud）；在 packages/sdk/server/tests/server.spec.ts 补 prompt-before-initialize 拒绝用例。
findings.title: 服务端默认 model 是 'deepseek-official'（与 provider 默认同值，疑似复制粘贴），且 initialize 前可 prompt

findings.detail: TS HarnessClient.close() 后 start() 抛 TransportClosedError（client.ts:222），RelayHarness.close 文档写明 terminal；Python close() 置 `_proc = None`、RelayHarness.close 重置 `_initialized`，随后 start() 会静默 spawn 新 runtime。另外 teardown 阶梯不同：TS 是 stdin-EOF 后 6s quiesce 宽限再 SIGTERM(3s)→SIGKILL（disposeEofGraceMs/disposeGraceMs 可配），Python 在 EOF 后仅等 shutdown_timeout_seconds（默认 1s）就 terminate→kill，无 EOF quiesce 窗口且不可配。同一消费代码在两个 SDK 上看到不同的关闭/重启行为与不同的优雅退出成功率。
findings.suggested_fix: 二选一对齐：要么 Python 也把 close 定为 terminal（置 closed 标志，start() 抛错），要么 TS 放开 restart 并改文档；给 Python 增加 eof_grace_seconds 配置并与 TS 默认值对齐，README 两侧同步。
findings.title: close/restart 生命周期语义不对称：Python close() 可重启，TS 永久关闭；teardown 宽限也差 6 倍

findings.detail: Python HarnessClient 维护 `_requests` 队列与 next_request()/respond()/respond_error()（bridge 部署需要，且有测试 test_client_routes_bridge_requests_and_sends_responses）；TS 设计孪生从未安装 transport.onRequest，JsonRpcLineTransport 对带 id+method 的入站帧自动回 -32601 method not found（transport.ts:322-324）。Python README 把这些称为 "Python-only low-level channels"，即已文档化的不对称——但代价是 TS SDK 完全不能接 bridge 形态的 runtime，且 HarnessSdkRequestMap（protocol/types.ts）没有 server→client 方向的声明，协议类型没有完整投影 wire。
findings.suggested_fix: 若 bridge 部署是当前需求，给 TS client 加 onRequest 订阅面（事件回调或 async iterator）并在 HarnessSdkRequestMap 补 server→client 方法映射；若明确不支持，在 packages/sdk/client README 与 protocol types 里写明 TS 侧对入站请求一律 -32601 的契约，避免被当成 bug 排查。
findings.title: TS SDK 无法消费 server→client 请求：transport 无 onRequest，一律回 -32601；Python 有完整 next_request/respond 面

findings.detail: 对应上面 2/3/4 号发现：(a) 无并发 start() 只 spawn 一个子进程的测试；(b) 无 subscribe-before-start + close 的挂起/失败断言；(c) Python 无 malformed initialize result 用例（TS 有 sdk-client.spec.ts:228）。另外快照面：TS 侧 notifications.expected.jsonl 逐场景钉住通知流，Python 侧仅 advanced/result.json（CI python-runtime job 独跑）包含 notifications，minimal 场景只钉 model-visible——只改通知 payload 的 SessionEventMap 变更在本地 Python 快照里不可见。
findings.suggested_fix: 在 python/sdk/tests/test_client.py 增加 test_concurrent_start_spawns_single_runtime、test_subscribe_before_start_then_close_fails_subscription、test_initialize_rejects_missing_server_info；TS 侧补 subscribe-before-start 用例到 packages/sdk/client/tests/sdk-client.spec.ts；AGENTS.md 的"Both SDKs project the loop"检查项中把 advanced/result.json 明确列为通知流的 Python 对应物。
findings.title: 测试缺口：并发 start、close-without-start 订阅、initialize 协议校验的 Python 侧均无用例

audits.summary: 两个 SDK（packages/sdk 的 TS 客户端与 python/sdk）确实是同一 wire 协议（newline-delimited JSON-RPC）的投影，队列有界（订阅队列、全局队列、incoming-request 队列、写队列、帧上限、stderr tail 均有界并在溢出时响亮失败），测试覆盖面大。但"design twin"已出现多处行为漂移：initialize 协议校验（Python 静默接受缺失 serverInfo，TS 抛 SdkProtocolError）、RunResult 投影（Python 有 finish_reason 且校验 turn/end，TS 没有；final_response 读取路径不同）、畸形 session.event 的错误传播（TS 抛错，Python 静默吞掉）、close/restart 生命周期语义（TS 永久关闭，Python 可重启）。Python 侧还有一个真实的 spawn 竞态（start() 的检查与 Popen 都在锁外）。共同的设计债是：server 端 sessions Map 无回收、协议无 session 关闭方法，而两个 SDK 的高层 run() 默认每次铸造新 session uuid，长驻 harness 会无限累积 agent。快照方面 TS 侧 4 个场景钉住 notifications.expected.jsonl，Python 侧仅 advanced 场景（CI-only）记录通知，minimal 只钉 model-visible 请求，parity 保护偏弱。

findings.detail: start() builds `pending = Promise.resolve().then(dispose).then(ok..., () => { forceExitOnce(code) })`. The rejection handler exits the process without writing the error anywhere (stderr, rlh log, or a distinct exit code). Consequence: when a headless one-shot's `ctx.fiber.dispose()` rejects, `shutdown.shutdown(0)` still completes naturally with exit 0 (and a SIGTERM-triggered shutdown force-exits 0), so a failed teardown is indistinguishable from a clean one. This also violates the repo rule that an empty catch names what it swallows — here the rejection is dropped with no name and no log.
findings.suggested_fix: In the rejection handler, write `process-shutdown: disposal failed: <message>` to stderr (or a logger parameter) before forceExitOnce, and consider exit code 1 on that path so callers can distinguish failed teardown.
findings.title: createProcessShutdown silently swallows disposal errors and still exits 0

findings.detail: handleHttp does `this.pending.set(id, {res})` and only deletes the entry when the desktop host sends an `http-end` frame or on host detach. There is (a) no timeout for a desktop that accepts the frame but never answers, and (b) no `res.on('close')` cleanup when the HTTP client aborts. On a long-running public relay (standalone shebang entry, `--cert/--key` deployment) each such request pins a pending entry and an open socket indefinitely; clients can accumulate unbounded entries (memory + FDs). Existing tests (src/main/remote.test.js) cover close() but not the hang/abort paths.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a per-request timeout that 504s and deletes the pending entry, and delete the entry on `res` close; cover both paths in apps/desktop/src/main/remote.test.js or a new apps/desktop/src/relay/server.test.js (colocated *.test.js convention, picked up by `pnpm run test:desktop`).
findings.title: RelayServer.pending grows without bound — no per-request timeout or client-disconnect cleanup

findings.detail: ensureOwnedPort calls killOwnedListeners whenever the wanted port answers HTTP, and RlhManager._doStop calls it on every stop. A listener is considered killable only if its image name matches /^(node|rlh)(\.exe)?$/ and it is not this Electron process — that is not proof the desktop owns it. A user's unrelated Node dev server (or another agent harness) on the default port 3080 is terminated via `taskkill /T /F` or process-group SIGTERM, destroying unrelated processes with no confirmation. The pid file narrows the first path but not the httpReady fallback. The non-Windows `process.kill(-pid)` also silently no-ops for non-group-leader children (falls back to single-pid kill), so the group-kill intent is only partly real.
findings.suggested_fix: Only kill listeners proven owned: the pid file, a child spawned this session, or a marker match on the HTTP response (e.g. the rlh web banner); otherwise hop to findFreePort. Add a test pinning that a foreign HTTP listener is NOT killed.
findings.title: Desktop kills arbitrary node/rlh processes listening on its configured port

findings.detail: workspace-authority.js documents that the allowlist exists so 'a third-party plugin installed through the marketplace must not be able to drive shell.gitPush or shell.readFile against an arbitrary directory using the user's credentials'. But marketplace client plugins execute in the same privileged harness BrowserView (apps/web/vite.config.ts comment: plugins 'arrive as runtime bundles through the client module system') where window.shell also exposes ptyCreate (interactive shell — full filesystem/credential access from any authorized cwd) and previewAutomationEvaluate (arbitrary JS in a page). The fs/git allowlist therefore provides no containment against the adversary the doc names.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restate the trust model honestly (harness renderer plugins are trusted with shell-equivalent power; the authority only guards path-handling bugs and non-plugin pages) in workspace-authority.js and the desktop README, or gate shell-capable channels (ptyCreate, previewAutomation*) behind a separate capability client plugins do not receive.
findings.title: Workspace-authority threat model is defeated by the same surface's shell-capable channels

findings.detail: readJson catches every parse/read failure and returns `{ ...fallback }` with no comment naming the swallow (violating the AGENTS.md empty-catch rule) and no loud failure. A corrupted config.json silently resets workspace/theme/restart policy; the next saveConfig persists those defaults, permanently destroying the user's settings. The same path applies to credentials.json (apiKey/githubToken). The tmp+rename writer makes corruption unlikely but not impossible (disk full, crash mid-rename, manual edit).
findings.suggested_fix: On JSON.parse failure of an existing file, log via rlh.log or a dialog and quarantine the bad file (e.g. config.json.corrupt-<ts>) instead of silently regenerating; per AGENTS.md 'misconfiguration fails loud', and the empty catch must at minimum name what it swallows.
findings.title: Corrupt config.json/credentials.json silently resets to defaults and the loss is then persisted

findings.detail: globalShortcut.register('CommandOrControl+Shift+I', ... toggleDevTools) intercepts the combo across the entire OS — even when the app is unfocused — and is armed unconditionally in packaged builds. It steals the shortcut from every other application and provides a system-wide toggle into DevTools of a privileged view. Every other window-level behavior in this app is correctly scoped (setWindowOpenHandler, will-navigate guards), so this global hook is an outlier on the Electron security/UX surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a window-scoped mechanism: a local menu accelerator, `webContents.on('before-input-event')`, or a focus-scoped shortcut, so the binding only applies while a Relay window is focused.
findings.title: OS-wide global shortcut registers a system-wide DevTools toggle in packaged builds

findings.detail: `shell:restart` and `shell:cancel-restart` are BOOT_ONLY, but `shell:retry-full-plugins` is ALL_SURFACES and its handler calls harness.retryFullPlugins() — i.e. clearPluginRecovery() + restart(). The launch smoke (index.js:539-543) asserts `harnessShellApiIsScoped: typeof api.restart === 'undefined'`, presenting surface scoping as a security property, while the harness preload's retryFullPlugins reaches the same operation. The asymmetry is unexplained (AGENTS.md: unexplained asymmetry signals a missed extraction).
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one policy: move retry-full-plugins to BOOT_ONLY (harness surface shows a 'restart required' state like the boot page), or document why restart is safe from the harness surface, and align the smoke's scoping assertion with the real boundary.
findings.title: Harness surface can restart via retry-full-plugins while the smoke advertises 'no restart on harness'

findings.detail: composeProfile/prepareProfile (parse profile layers, the user cordis.patch.yml, --patch overlays) run at profile-boot.ts:226 before installFailLoud is installed at line 241. A malformed user patch file — exactly the 'misconfiguration fails loud at load' class fail-loud exists for — surfaces as Node's raw unhandled-rejection dump instead of the `rlh: fatal load failure:` formatter with its release hook, inconsistent with failures after boot() starts.
findings.suggested_fix: Install installFailLoud (or apply the same stderr formatting) before composeProfile runs in runProfile, so the entire startup window reports through one channel.
findings.title: installFailLoud installed after composeProfile — load-time misconfigurations bypass fail-loud formatting

findings.detail: RlhManager.buildLaunch composes `web --skip-user-plugins --patch ... --host --port --no-open` as bare strings. The consumer lives in a different package/process (packages/bundle/web-app/src/startup.ts), and each side is tested only against its own copy of the literal (apps/desktop/src/main/rlh.test.js:495-517 pins the producer; web-app tests pin the consumer). No single contract pins both: renaming a flag in web-app's startup parser leaves the desktop spawning a process whose flag is silently ignored, failing only via the 180s readiness timeout with a generic message.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the desktop→`rlh web` flag contract in apps/cli/composition.md (or export the flag names from rlh-app-boot) and add one cross-app assertion (a web-app test importing the shared names, or a desktop test grepping the web-app startup source) so a rename fails a gate instead of a boot.
findings.title: Desktop→`rlh web` flag contract is stringly-typed with only producer-side pins

findings.detail: The self-hosted relay's forwarding is tested for the happy path and close(), but nothing exercises the two leak paths identified in the audit: (a) host accepts an http frame and never replies — the pending entry and client socket are held forever; (b) the HTTP client aborts before http-end — the pending entry should be reclaimed. Following the repo's colocated convention this belongs in apps/desktop/src/main/remote.test.js (which already constructs RelayServer) or a new apps/desktop/src/relay/server.test.js; `pnpm run test:desktop` already globs src/**/*.test.js.
findings.suggested_fix: Add two node:test cases: a fake host that swallows an http frame → assert a bounded-timeout 504 and pending cleanup (after the fix); and a client socket destroyed mid-request → assert `pending.size === 0`.
findings.title: Test gap: relay pending-request timeout and client-disconnect reclamation

audits.summary: The three entry apps are deliberately thin and unusually well hardened. apps/cli is a ~1k-line launcher (args, profile-boot, plugin, dump-config) that delegates all composition to rlh-app-boot and has strong colocated test coverage; apps/web is a 10-line Vite bootstrap over @relay-harness/rlh-client-web with a careful chunking/dedupe build config; apps/desktop is the real mass — 124 main-process modules composing an Electron shell that spawns `rlh web` as a child, mounts the UI in a sandboxed, contextIsolated BrowserView, and guards IPC by sender role, loopback-origin allowlists, workspace-root authority, renderer-writable config field validation, and sanitized download paths. Cross-app duplication is minimal (each app owns exactly one seam: CLI composes, web renders, desktop launches and embeds), and the desktop's pid/generation fencing around the child process is carefully done. The remaining issues sit at the edges: a silent error swallow plus exit-0 masking in the shared process-shutdown controller, unbounded pending-request growth in the standalone relay server, an unowned-process kill path on port conflicts, a system-wide DevTools shortcut, a corrupt-config silent-reset data-loss path, and a workspace-authority threat model that its own PTY channel defeats.

findings.detail: LocalJobRegistry.store (packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts:102) only removes records in disposeOwned (line 471, fired when the owner Agent's scope disposes) and disposeAll (line 494, service teardown). There is no prune of terminal records: a completed/failed/killed job owned by a long-lived agent stays in the store for the agent's lifetime, and a job started with owner undefined (JobStart.owner is optional, packages/jobs/jobs/src/types.ts:62) has NO deletion path at all — disposeOwned filters `job.owner === owner`, so unowned rows survive even owner disposal. In the long-lived Host this grows without bound, and `list()` (line 192, the model-facing job list surface) keeps returning every historical snapshot, inflating model-visible output forever. The existing test only pins bounded retention of wait resolvers while a job is live (packages/jobs/jobs-local/tests/jobs.spec.ts:105), not store growth.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a retention policy for terminal records: delete (or stop listing) a job once it is terminal and reported, e.g. drop on the next list()/start() sweep after `reported && finishedAt + graceMs`, with a bounded completed-records cap per owner. Add packages/jobs/jobs-local/tests/jobs-retention.spec.ts covering: completed unowned job removed, completed owned job removed while owner still live, and job_output of a pruned id failing loud.
findings.title: jobs-local never prunes terminal job records; unowned jobs leak for the process lifetime

findings.detail: ctx.on('agent/turn-stopping') (packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:270-277) steers a continuation message whenever the merged Stop-hook outcome is deny, with no counter and no signal that the previous continuation was itself hook-forced. A hook that always answers {decision:'deny'} (or is misconfigured to) makes the machine run model steps forever — each iteration spends a provider request. The file acknowledges this at line 269 (TODO(stop-loop-guard)) and hooks-codex carries the same gap (packages/hooks/hooks-codex/src/index.ts:254). For a hook bridge whose whole point is running untrusted user scripts, 'hooks must self-limit meanwhile' is not an enforcement: the enforcement happens in the operation that makes the decision (packages/AGENTS.md).
findings.suggested_fix: Cap consecutive hook-forced continuations per turn (a Config field, e.g. maxForcedContinuations, failing loud or converting to a normal stop with a model-visible notice when exhausted). Mirror in hooks-codex, and add a test that a deny-looping Stop hook terminates after the cap in packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/tests/.
findings.title: Blocking Stop hooks force unbounded continuations with no loop guard (per-hook scripts can burn unbounded model spend)

findings.detail: With a crash (or kill -9) between writeFile(lockPath) and the finally rm (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:112-129), `<file>.lock` persists. Every subsequent writer then retries for LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS (2s) and throws 'timed out waiting for the writer lock' — forever. The lock file contains the owner pid (line 114) but isLockContention never consults it. For LocalCredentialProvider this is the write path for every credential (packages/credentials/credentials-local/src/index.ts:394): one crashed writer permanently bricks credential set/unset until the user manually deletes the lock. The code comments name orphan recovery as an operator action, but the pid is sitting in the file and a same-host liveness check (process.kill(pid, 0)) would self-heal the overwhelmingly common case (same machine, dead writer) without weakening the cross-process protocol.
findings.suggested_fix: On EEXIST/EPERM-contention, read the pid from the lock; when the pid is not alive (ESRCH from process.kill(pid,0)) and the lock is on the same host boot, remove the stale lock and retry. Keep failing loud for foreign-host or unreadable locks. Add a packages/util/atomic-write/tests test for stale-lock recovery.
findings.title: Orphaned writer lock in rlh-atomic-write permanently bricks credentials/settings writes until manual operator action

findings.detail: apply() fills sessions only in newSession (packages/acp/acp/src/index.ts:326) and clears it only in quiesce (lines 454-455, on connection close). The implemented Agent surface (initialize/authenticate/newSession/prompt/cancel) has no per-session unload, and the bridge registers none. Each record pins a live Agent plus its in-memory session log for the connection's lifetime, so a long-lived automation client that creates a session per task accumulates agents, session state, and durable-output work indefinitely while the connection stays open. Same map also has no cap, so a buggy client can create unbounded sessions.
findings.suggested_fix: Either implement the ACP session-unload/setSessionMode family to dispose the record (dispose the handle and delete from the map), or add a Config-bounded max live sessions per connection (reject newSession loudly when exceeded, per 'misconfiguration fails loud'). Add an acp tests case that a disposed/unloaded session is removed from the map.
findings.title: ACP bridge keeps every created session (live Agent + in-memory log) until the whole connection closes

findings.detail: In 'half-open', record() (packages/guard/llm-circuit-breaker/src/breaker.ts:81-85) unconditionally `probes.shift()`s and, on success, close()s the breaker. But probes only contain slots claimed via check() after the state transitioned; requests admitted while the breaker was closed (check() passes immediately, no probe recorded) can settle after the trip and reach record() in half-open. A stale in-flight success therefore consumes a probe slot and closes the breaker before any real probe outcome lands, and a stale failure trips on a slot it never claimed. Wired per provider in packages/guard/llm-circuit-breaker/src/index.ts:110-116, so every provider request is exposed. Separately, closed-state samples (line 74) are evicted only by age (windowMs default 60s), with no count cap, so a high request rate accumulates the whole window's outcomes in memory.
findings.suggested_fix: Track in-flight requests admitted in closed state (or stamp each request with the state at check() time) and route record() by that stamp: non-probe outcomes recorded in half-open should update samples or be ignored, never shift a probe slot. Add a max-samples cap (drop-oldest beyond N) to bound memory. Extend packages/guard/llm-circuit-breaker/tests with a trip-while-in-flight case.
findings.title: CircuitBreaker half-open accounting lets stale closed-state outcomes consume probe slots and close early; samples uncapped within window

findings.detail: listDirectory (packages/fs/fs-local/src/fsio.ts:282-321) awaits, per child, resolveListedChildTarget → resolveLocalTarget → realpath (line 151) and then probe → stat bigint (line 307), strictly sequentially (`for … await`). A directory with a few thousand entries costs 2n sequential syscalls plus n promise ticks before the tool can render anything. Entries are also fully resolved (each child's own realpath) even though callers only need names/types/sizes for listing — the deep resolution only matters for identity keys that the caller may never use.
findings.suggested_fix: Either resolve children concurrently with a small bounded pool, or make the deep child resolution lazy (resolve the identity key only when the consumer asks for a child target) and build listing rows from the Dirent plus one lstat. Keep abort checks per batch.
findings.title: fs-local listDirectory does two sequential syscalls (realpath + bigint stat) per child on the model-facing list path

findings.detail: privateSpillDir() (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts:89-92) creates one 0700 tmpdir per process and never removes it; OutputCollector spill logs (rlh-subprocess-<pid>-<n>-<rand>-<label>.log, up to maxSpillBytes each — bash-local defaults to 64MB per stream, packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:38) are only unlinked in the discardSpill overflow path (line 176). On normal settlement the file is deliberately kept (it is advertised as spillPath), and nothing removes it at service teardown or process exit. Repeated overflowing commands (e.g. `cat` of a huge file through the bash tool) leave tens of MB per run in /tmp across many sessions.
findings.suggested_fix: Track created spill paths per process and remove them at composition teardown (the owning service already has a host-exit hook: terminateForHostExit), or age-prune the rlh-subprocess-* directory on the next process start using the same retention helper other packages use.
findings.title: subprocess spill files are never cleaned up after the process exits

findings.suggested_fix: Keep a rolling decoded-string tail with a byte cursor, or cache the concatenated Buffer keyed by total and invalidate on push, so repeated polls between chunks are O(1).
findings.title: OutputCollector.readFrom re-concatenates the whole retained tail on every read
findings.detail: readFrom does `Buffer.concat(this.chunks)` then a UTF-8 decode of the slice on each call. bash-local's background readOutput (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:289-309) calls it for both streams on every job_output poll while a job runs, so continuous polling of a chatty job is O(tail) copy+decode per poll, per stream. The in-memory cap is config (maxOutputBytes), so raising it from the 64KB default multiplies the cost linearly.

createExecutor calls assertToolResultSize(result, …) (packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/tools.ts:345, 389-400) which JSON.stringify's the entire untrusted result purely to measure it, before extractText/projects it (which serializes or walks the same data again). A server returning a result just under maxToolResultBytes (default 4MB) pays an extra full serialization plus a transient string of the same size on every call; an oversized result pays full serialization before rejection. The JSON-RPC transport has already buffered the raw response, so this is a doubling, not the first copy.
findings.suggested_fix: Measure size without materializing the full string (e.g. a counting JSON serializer that aborts once the budget is exceeded, or size the raw transport frame when available) and only stringify once for the error message on the rejection path.
findings.title: MCP tool bridge serializes every untrusted result twice: once to measure, once to use

findings.detail: The `title` parameter of Workspace.create survives only for a deleted gateway branch, with an in-code TODO (packages/workspace/workspace/src/index.ts:168-172) to drop the parameter, its @param clause, and the README lines. Until removed, every caller can pass a title that is silently ignored for existing workspaces and only used on first creation — an API surface the code does not enforce a meaning for.
findings.suggested_fix: Execute the recorded TODO: drop `title` from create() and update the package README pair in the same commit (pre-release stance allows the breaking rename).
findings.title: workspace.create(title?) is a documented dead parameter kept on a public service signature

findings.detail: writeFileAtomic documents 'Crash durability (fsync) is out of scope' (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:44) with TODO(settings-atomic-durability) at line 54. LocalCredentialProvider relies on it for its authoritative secret store (packages/credentials/credentials-local/src/index.ts:404, 489): a crash or power loss after the rename but before writeback can leave .credentials.yaml empty or stale while the in-process notifyUpdated already reported success to listeners. The seam's contract docs promise durability semantics ('durably store one value', packages/credentials/credentials/src/index.ts:83) without qualifying the fsync gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Either fsync file (and parent dir on POSIX) in the shared primitive before rename, or qualify the rlh-credentials Service Definition JSDoc and credentials-local README with the crash-window so consumers know the stored value is not crash-durable.
findings.title: Credentials and settings durability depends on an unfixed no-fsync atomic write

findings.detail: Every deep-audited package (fs-local, bash-local, subprocess-local, mcp-client, acp, credentials-local) carries behavior specs, but three verified failure paths have no home: (a) LocalBashExecutor.startArgv's spawn-failure note surfacing exactly once through readOutput and status='killed' (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:262-288); (b) mcp syncTools phase-2 foreign-namespace conflict rollback leaving zero tools registered and the next sync recovering (packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/tools.ts:203-215) — connection.ts's give-up disposal depends on this; (c) credentials-local STABLE_READ_ATTEMPTS exhaustion ('document kept changing while reading') propagating as a write failure while a reload only warns (packages/credentials/credentials-local/src/index.ts:558-578). These are the paths where a regression silently breaks live tool bridges and secret writes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add packages/shell/bash-local/tests/bash-background-spawn-failure.spec.ts, packages/mcp/mcp-client/tests/sync-conflict-rollback.spec.ts, and a moving-file case in packages/credentials/credentials-local/tests covering both the write (throws) and reload (warns, keeps last good) policies.
findings.title: Bounded-spill and lossy-read behavior of long-running background shells lacks failure-path specs (test gap)

audits.summary: The infra/tooling slice is unusually disciplined: credentials-local, fs-local/fs-sandbox, subprocess-local, and mcp-client all document their race windows, fail loud on misconfiguration, and bound untrusted output (spill caps, catalog caps, byte limits). The real defects cluster in lifecycle retention rather than protocol logic: jobs-local never prunes terminal job records (unowned jobs leak for the process lifetime), the ACP bridge keeps every created session until the whole connection closes, and hooks-claude-code/codex turn a deny-looping Stop hook into unbounded forced continuations. Two durability/availability edges sit in util/atomic-write, which both credentials and settings depend on: an orphaned `.lock` file permanently bricks writes, and there is no fsync behind the "durable" credential store. Remaining findings are hot-path costs (per-read tail re-concatenation, double serialization of MCP results, two sequential syscalls per child in listDirectory).

findings.detail: packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:377-383: 当 phase.step === 0 且 pre-step waterfall 把 decision 重写为 {kind:'enter', messages: []} 时，turn() 直接 `return false`，跳过了其他所有出口都执行的尾部逻辑（agent.ts:437-442 的 `if (!this.inbox.hasPending) return false; ... return true`）。Inbox.claim(target='next-turn') 只消费 1 条 next-turn 消息加全部 next-step（packages/core/agent/src/inbox.ts:101-108），且运行中驱动的 wake 不设 wakeRequested 锁存（agent.ts:231-241 'Live drivers claim queued work themselves'）。因此：send('a'); send('b') 后监听器返回空 enter，turn 1 认领 'a' 并以 completed 关闭，'b' 仍留在 inbox 里但驱动已退出、无锁存、无重唤——消息被静默搁置直到下一次外部 wakeup。对比兄弟分支 `if (turnEnds && decision.messages.length === 0) break`（第 377 行）走 break 后会经过尾部 hasPending 检查，两条路径行为不对称。现有测试 contract-regressions.spec.ts:190 'closes an empty admitted batch as a turn without a step' 只覆盖单条消息场景（断言 nextTurn 为空恰因唯一消息已被认领），未覆盖残留排队输入。
findings.suggested_fix: 把 `return false` 改为与兄弟分支一致地落到尾部收尾（例如先设 turnEnds 再 break，或在 return 前复用 `if (!this.inbox.hasPending) return false` + 置新 AbortController/重置 step 的续转逻辑），使空 enter 与其他 turn 出口共享同一个 hasPending 重查/续转路径。补回归测试到 packages/core/agent-loop/tests/contract-regressions.spec.ts（紧邻既有 empty-batch 用例）：两条 followup + 空 enter 监听器，断言第二条消息开新 turn。
findings.title: 空 enter 决策使已排队的 inbox 输入永久搁置（跳过 hasPending 重查与续转）

findings.detail: 同一段「解析 listener 快照 → 逐个调用 → 同步 throw 用 logger.warn 吞掉 → 返回的 Promise reject 也用 logger.warn 吞掉」的模式至少有 6 份手写实现：agent/dispatch.ts:120-137（emit，并自称是唯一拼法）、agent/index.ts:528-540（emitDisposed）与 562-571（announce）、session/index.ts:419-437（invokeContainedSessionObservers）、session/index.ts:1044-1057（announce）、agent-loop/index.ts:430-441（reportConfiguredStartupFailure，因事件非 agent-subject 而绕开 dispatch.ts 重新手写）、tools/index.ts:1944-1964（notifyResult）。六份实现行为一致但注释、日志格式和错误字符串化方式（String(error) vs errorChain）各自漂移；agent-loop 里那份正是因为没有一个可复用的非 agent-subject 包含式 emit 才重复的。
findings.suggested_fix: 在一个低层包（rlh-scope 或 rlh-llm 旁的 util 面）导出一个 `emitContained(ctx, thisArg, name, args, warn: (msg) => void)` 帮助函数，六处调用点收敛到它；session/flush 的「抛出而非包含」变体保留在 SessionStore.flush（语义不同，有注释说明）。这与 AGENTS.md 'Prefer symmetry for parallel values; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction' 直接对应。
findings.title: 「包含式 emit」模式在 core 内重复实现约 6 处，语义各自漂移

findings.detail: agent.ts:102-111 从 session.events 末尾向前线性扫描寻找 'agent-preset/selected'；找不到时（绝大多数会话）每次 preStep 都完整遍历整个事件日志——包括每个 assistant/chunk。事件数随会话无界增长，单步 O(n)、全会话 O(n²)。同文件的 requestHeader()/deriveMessages() 都已用「增量 fold 到已见位置」的模式（session/index.ts:712-741），此处是未解释的不对称。
findings.suggested_fix: 仿照 requestHeader 的增量 fold：ReactLoopAgent 持有一个 lastPresetScanSeq/lastPreset 游标，每步只扫描新增事件并保留最新 selected 值（事件只追加，前向 fold 即可得到与反向扫描等价的结果），构造时一次性从尾部扫到当前长度作为初值。
findings.title: currentAgentPreset 每个模型步全量回扫事件日志，长会话 O(n²)

findings.detail: inbox.ts:236-268 每次拼接都执行：`inbox.toSpliced`（整表复制）、跨两个 pending 列表重建消息 id Set（O(pending)，上限 4096）、并对所有 removed 消息重新 JSON.stringify 计算字节数。claim()（每次模型步的步前边界）也走同一 validate，意味着每个 step 都要把本步认领的全部输入（可能是几十 KB 的 prompt）重新序列化一遍，只为维持字节账目——而 inserted 的字节数在插入时已经算过，removed 的字节数是完全可缓存的。突发写入时每条消息成本 O(已排队量)，4096 条排队下一次突发为 O(n²)。
findings.suggested_fix: 为每条 pending 消息在插入时用 WeakMap 缓存 serializedMessageBytes 结果，removed 字节直接查缓存；id 唯一性可改为随 splice 增量维护的两个 Set（插入/删除同步增删），去掉每次的 toSpliced 全表复制。容量语义不变，仅消除重复计算。
findings.title: Inbox.validate 每次拼接 O(pending) 重建 Set + 整表复制，且 claim 每步重新 JSON 序列化已认领消息

findings.detail: 同一个持久错误码 TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN 有两种模型可见文本：(1) session/src/repair.ts:19 的 TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN_TEXT（长版，含「仅在只读/幂等时重试、先验证外部状态」的完整指导），被崩溃恢复 closers（repair.ts:109）和 tool-transcript.ts:147-162 的派生期合成结果使用；(2) agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:373-385 的 appendOutcomeUnknown 在调度器终态失败路径写入一段自带的短文本（'...verify external state before retrying'），错误码相同但指导措辞不同。模型在同一会话内可能先后通过两条路径看到同一代码的两种说法；tool-calls.ts 完全可以引用 rlh-session 已导出的常量（该包已依赖 TOOL_NOT_STARTED/TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN 码）。
findings.suggested_fix: tool-calls.ts 的 appendOutcomeUnknown 改用 rlh-session 导出的 TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN_TEXT（export 已存在，repair.ts:30），使同一恢复码在崩溃恢复、派生合成、调度器失败三条路径上产生逐字节相同的模型可见文本；快照面若受影响按 testing 政策同步更新。
findings.title: TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN 的模型可见文本在三条恢复路径上不一致

findings.detail: contract-regressions.spec.ts:190-207 现有 'closes an empty admitted batch as a turn without a step' 只发送单条消息且被 claim 消费，断言 nextTurn 为空——这恰因没有残留输入而通过。它没有覆盖：空 enter 决策落下时 inbox 中仍有 next-turn/next-step 残留（监听器返回空期间 followup/steer 到达，或排队第二条 turn 消息）。这是上面 bug 发现的直接验证缺口；该 spec 文件正是此类空 enter 回归的既定家。
findings.suggested_fix: 在 packages/core/agent-loop/tests/contract-regressions.spec.ts 增加一个用例：预置两条 followup（或空 enter 决策挂起期间 followup），断言驱动收敛后第二条消息在自己的 turn 中被认领并产生 step/start（修复后应通过，修复前失败），沿用现有 harness/send/waitForIdle 工具函数。
findings.title: 空 enter 决策 + 排队残留输入的组合无回归测试覆盖

audits.summary: packages/core（agent-loop / agent / session / tools / system-prompt / scope / agent-default-model / agent-tool-presentation，约 49k 行）整体工程质量很高：生命周期用单一可 memoize 的反向 teardown、fused AbortController 和「先注册后发布」的事务边界覆盖了竞态；Session 的 append/surface/deriveMessages 增量 fold 与 model-visible⟺logged 不变量在代码和 JSDoc 中贯彻得很一致；tool 调度器的 abort/scheduler-failure 配对保证转录始终 provider-valid（interruptedBlocks 确实剔除 tool-call 块，与事件文档一致）。审计发现的实际问题集中在两处边界：agent-loop 的空 enter 决策提前 return 绕过了所有其他 turn 出口共有的 inbox.hasPending 重查，可在文档化的 pre-step 扩展点下静默搁置已入队消息；此外是若干热路径的 O(n) 重复扫描/序列化和一处跨包复制的「包含式 emit」模式。未发现无界增长、错误吞没或 id branding 违规。

findings.detail: connection/src/client/index.ts:9 statically imports FixtureApiClient from ./fixture.ts (3,335 lines embedding a 74-turn hand-built history script plus rlh-session/llm folding helpers). The import is gated only at runtime by a `?fixture` query-param check (index.ts:88-91), so the entire fixture — and the tree of value imports it pulls (rlh-llm/message folding, rlh-session/surface folding) — lands in every production client bundle even though production always takes the WebApiClient path. Verified: the import is unconditional and the tsdown config has no fixture split.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the fixture branch a dynamic import: `const fixtureClient = fixture ? await (await import('./fixture.ts')).FixtureApiClient : undefined` inside an async plugin body (or a lazy subpath export like `@relay-harness/rlh-client-connection/fixture` imported only when the query param is present). The apply body is already allowed to be async-adjacent via ctx.effect; alternatively decide the transport one level up in web/boot where an await is free.
findings.title: 3,300-line dev FixtureApiClient is statically imported into the production browser bundle

findings.detail: Session keeps `events: SessionEvent[]` and `views: (ToolEventView|undefined)[]` (session.ts:67-70) and appends to both on every live frame (session.ts:675-676, acceptLiveEvent→appendLive); ConversationNodeAssembler keeps `inputs: Map<number, ConversationEventInput>` and `contextsBySeq: Map<number, Set>` (conversation-assembler.ts:140-141) with one entry per seq forever. The arrays/maps are only reset on replaceWindow (open/resync/gap-repair/loadOlder prepend), never trimmed during ordinary live streaming. For a long-running session (token-delta events stream one per chunk), a tab left open overnight accumulates the entire session tail in memory — this is the only unbounded-growth path in an otherwise carefully bounded slice (pendingBuffers compact by identity, entryCache/prevRunning are pruned, removedIds is tombstone-bounded).
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a client-side window cap (e.g. N most-recent events, mirroring the host tail-page model): when appending pushes past the cap, drop the oldest prefix, bump baseSeq/hasMore, and clear the corresponding assembler inputs/contextsBySeq entries plus retired contexts. Contexts whose dependencies fall outside the window already degrade via the `windowGap` dependency flag (conversation-assembler.ts:599), so the reader contract has a seam for this; document the chosen cap as a Config field per the no-hardcoded-tunables rule.
findings.title: Session event window grows without bound during a long-lived stream

findings.detail: SessionManager.questionInteractionStatus (manager.ts:91-103) re-implements ui-user-questions's binary plan-review classification (single question + intent.kind==='plan-review' + non-multiSelect + <=2 options including the approve label) to decide the sidebar's 'plan-review' amber-dot status. The manager comment explicitly says it must 'Match ui-user-questions's binary plan-review routing at the wire boundary' — i.e. correctness rests on a human keeping two copies in sync across two packages with no shared type or test linking them. If the composer's shape rule changes (e.g. multi-select plan reviews become plan-review cards), the sidebar keeps classifying them as plain questions.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the classifier to one pure function — `planReviewStatusOf(questions): PendingInteractionStatus` in runtime's sessions/pending.ts (where PendingInteractionStatus already lives) — and have ui-user-questions's composer shape selection consume the same predicate from `@relay-harness/rlh-client-runtime/client` (a type-safe existing dependency edge: ui-user-questions already type-imports the runtime). Add a shared unit test in runtime/tests/pending.client.spec.ts pinning both consumers' agreement.
findings.title: plan-review vs question routing rule duplicated between runtime manager and ui-user-questions composer

findings.detail: WebApiClient.readWebSocket (web-api-client.ts:45-101) is the browser's only wire parser: it JSON-parses every server frame against serverRequestSchema + frame schemas, drops malformed frames with console.error and continues, drains a wake-based inbox queue, handles abort during CONNECTING/OPEN, and closes the socket in its finally. None of this is under test — connection/tests has host-side websocket-downlink.host.spec.ts and http-bridge.host.spec.ts, but no client-side spec. The malformed-frame drop-and-continue path and the `if (signal.aborted) handleAbort()` pre-connect arm are exactly the kind of wire-boundary behavior AGENTS.md says to prove with an invalid-case rejection.
findings.suggested_fix: Add packages/client/connection/tests/web-api-client.client.spec.ts with a stubbed global WebSocket (message/close/open event targets) covering: malformed JSON rejected without ending the stream; schema-invalid payload dropped while a following valid frame still yields; abort during CONNECTING closes and ends the generator; abort during OPEN closes the socket; close-before-open ends the iterator. Follow the existing vi.stubGlobal pattern used in runtime/tests/notifier.client.spec.ts.
findings.title: No test covers the client WebSocket frame pump (WebApiClient.readWebSocket)

findings.detail: The readiness timeout (streamOpenTimeoutMs, connection.ts:185-187) only bounds the wait for onOpen; after it fires the loop still does `await failed` (connection.ts:189), which resolves only when both pumpStream generators end. A WebSocket that accepts TCP but never completes the WS handshake fires neither open nor close, so its generator sits in `await new Promise(resolve => { wake = resolve })` (web-api-client.ts:92) and `failed` never settles — no reconnect, no state change, frames dead. Browsers usually fire close on failed upgrades, but a half-open relay/proxy can park this for the OS TCP timeout (minutes). Related: the unary `host.describe({})` at connection.ts:142 takes no AbortSignal, so stop() cannot cancel an in-flight handshake and a stopped controller lingers until it settles.
findings.suggested_fix: Race `failed` against a second sleep (e.g. a generous connectionSettleTimeoutMs derived from streamOpenTimeoutMs) after the streamsOpen race, treating timeout as generation failure (`ac.abort()` → recover). Pass `ac.signal` into `host.describe` so stop()/failure paths cancel the unary handshake too.
findings.title: Reconnect loop can park indefinitely in `await failed` when a WebSocket never fires close

findings.detail: ConnectionHandle.start() stops the previous loop then starts a new controller immediately (client/index.ts:117-149). stop() aborts the old AbortController, but the old readWebSocket generators may already hold parsed frames in their `inbox` and the old pumpStream may be mid-`callSink`; those frames are delivered to the shared sinks after the new generation's describe/streams are underway, with no ordering guarantee against the new generation's replayed baseline frames (e.g. an old `session/queue` snapshot landing after the new `session/subscribed` reset). The effect is bounded (old sockets close on abort) but the window is real and the frame types involved are exactly the generation-scoped ones handleDisconnected/reset exist to police.
findings.suggested_fix: Make stop() drain: have ConnectionController.stop() capture the pumps' settlement (the `failed` promise or per-pump onEnd) and let ConnectionHandle.start() await the previous controller's drain before controller.start() of the replacement — or stamp each sink invocation with the controller instance and drop frames from a non-active controller in the client/index.ts sink wrappers.
findings.title: Old connection generation's buffered frames can still reach sinks after start() replacement

findings.detail: The `selection` field JSDoc (service.ts:252-258) states the projection 'validates it against the live list instead of destructively pruning, so a selection survives transient list states (reconnect re-pull) and resurfaces when its session returns'. projectList (service.ts:737-741) actually wipes the persisted cell via `this.selection.set({})` whenever `current === undefined` — which is exactly the masked-gap state — leaving only the in-memory `manager.selected` alive; a reload during that window lands on the empty state. The clear() doc (service.ts:420-423) describes the wipe as intended for user-initiated clear, but the same path fires for any masked current. Either the survival promise is overstated or the wipe is too eager; the two comments assert different contracts for the same cell.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one contract and document it in both places. If the wipe is intended only for durable removal/user clear, gate it on the manager reporting the session as gone (e.g. only wipe when the id is absent from `items` after a `phase === 'ready'` pull with no list error), and keep the masked-gap case persisted; otherwise soften the `selection` JSDoc to 'the in-memory selection survives transient gaps; the persisted cell does not'.
findings.title: SessionRuntime.selection JSDoc contradicts the persisted-cell wipe in projectList

findings.detail: hmr/src/client/index.ts:83-91 copies isLoopbackHostname (connection/src/loopback-hostname.ts:12-18) verbatim, documented as deliberate to avoid an immediately-tier plugin importing another client plugin. But the predicate is a pure zero-dep function and packages/util is the repo's designated zero-dependency shared home; as-is, a future loopback-rule change (e.g. IPv6 `::1` unbracketed, or 127/8 handling) must be made in two places or the HMR gate and the trust fence diverge silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Relocate the predicate to `@relay-harness/rlh-util` (or a client-shared pure module both packages already depend on) and re-export from connection; both halves import the single definition. Update the hmr comment that currently documents the duplication.
findings.title: Loopback predicate duplicated verbatim between hmr and connection

findings.detail: claimStyles (system.ts:34-44) tags every `style:not([data-plugin])` element on the page with the materializing plugin's id, and HMR later removes owned tags by that id (hmr/src/client/index.ts:102-106). Anything else that injects an untagged inline <style> (a dev tool panel, a third-party widget, a future non-plugin stylesheet) between two plugin materializations is silently adopted by whichever plugin materializes next — then deleted wholesale when that plugin hot-reloads. The claim window is the synchronous materialize() call, so the practical exposure is styles injected by earlier non-materializing code paths, but the ownership rule is 'untagged at that instant' rather than 'injected by this factory'.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the claim: have the css injection convention pre-tag every plugin-emitted style (the comment says preset-emitted tags already arrive tagged) and treat untagged tags as an error logged loudly (fail-loud per AGENTS.md) instead of adopting them — or snapshot `document.querySelectorAll('style')` immediately before factory execution and claim only the diff, which is exactly the factory's own emission set.
findings.title: Module system claims every untagged <style> tag for the materializing plugin

audits.summary: The web frontend core (connection controller, runtime object layer, module system, HMR, locale) is unusually disciplined: reconnect/resume is handled through generation-scoped state resets (manager.handleDisconnected → handleConnected → per-session resync with openGeneration invalidation, seq-guarded projection stores, queue-mirror re-baselining on session/subscribed), snapshots are identity-stable for useSyncExternalStore, and registries dispose through ctx.effect. The strongest issues found are bundle-weight (a 3,300-line dev fixture statically imported into the production entry), an unbounded per-session event window that grows for the tab's lifetime during long-running streams, a knowingly duplicated plan-review classification rule shared with ui-user-questions, and a complete absence of tests for the client-side WebSocket frame pump. No lifecycle leak or listener-disposal bug survived verification: listener sets, caches, and maps in this slice all have documented prune paths.

findings.detail: Lyra's files tab is a real editor: CodeMirror 6 with per-language packages, search, wrap toggle, and overlay scrollbars (Lyra packages/desktop/package.json lines 27-55; README 面板 section '编辑器：语法高亮、自动换行开关、横竖两条滚动条'). relay-harness's counterpart renders file content in a bare <textarea> — packages/client/ui-files/src/client/FilePreview.tsx line 224 (`const textareaRef = useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement>(null)`), with reveal logic scrolling 'the source textarea' (lines 176-177). For a repo whose tool outputs are code, the Files panel is the main read surface for user-authored files; no highlighting and no wrap control is a visible capability gap against the Lyra bar. relay already ships shiki + @shikijs/langs in ui-primitives, so a highlighted read path needs no new heavy dependency.
findings.suggested_fix: Phase 1: replace the read-only textarea body in FilePreview.tsx with a shiki-highlighted <pre> layer (shiki is already a ui-primitives dependency) keeping the existing revealLine/revealRequestId scroll contract. Phase 2 only if editing is a real use case: adopt @codemirror/state+view (as Lyra does) for the edit surface. Add tests/ui-files FilePreview spec asserting reveal still scrolls to the requested line after the swap.
findings.title: Files panel has no syntax-highlighted editor — plain textarea vs Lyra's CodeMirror 6 file editor

findings.detail: Lyra AGENTS.md lines 27-52 codify, with four concrete past failures, that green lint/typecheck/unit tests do not prove user-visible behavior: a zoom animation that measured its own transformed box (scale computed as 1), tooltips wired via data-ly-tip but read as dataset.dwTip, a transition mounted on an element React unmounts, and icons broken by img-src — all invisible to static checks. The mandated remedy is measuring the running app: width sampling, pixel hashes, getComputedStyle, motion probes (Lyra desktop/e2e contains capture-motion-probe.ts, light-theme-probe.ts, scrollbar.test.ts, tab-flicker-probe.ts, transcript-perf.ts). relay-harness's gates are 100% per-file unit coverage plus DOM-structural e2e; apps/web/tests/complex-history.perf.ts lines 1-3 explicitly 'reports measurements without timing assertions', and nothing asserts the *visual* output of the new Relay Focus visual system (ui-theme derive.ts declares contrast floors NAV_ITEM_ACTIVE_MIN_CONTRAST=1.25 / NAV_ITEM_ACTIVE_ACCENT_MIN_CONTRAST=1.4 at lines 23-28 that no test verifies against the rendered cascade).
findings.suggested_fix: Add two probe-style e2e files following the existing apps/web/tests naming: (1) appearance-derived-tokens.e2e.ts — seed a custom theme family, read computed --rlw-* tokens off :root via getComputedStyle, assert the nav-active contrasts meet the derive.ts floors in both light and dark halves; (2) motion-reduced-motion.e2e.ts — emulate prefers-reduced-motion, assert transition durations on a [data-rlh-motion] popover are the zeroed tokens. Both fit the existing launchWebScaffold harness (apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts) and stay keyless.
findings.title: No 'measure the rendered app' probe suite: visual regressions pass all gates (Lyra's core testing lesson)

findings.detail: Both codebases zero motion under the OS preference, but only Lyra surfaces it as a setting: 外观 offers 减少动态效果 (system / on / off) and enforces it app-wide (README 外观 section; packages/desktop/src/motion-freeze.ts). relay-harness honors only the media query — packages/client/ui-theme/src/styles/base.css line 113 `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` zeros the duration tokens, and THEME_SETTINGS fields (ui-theme/src/theme-settings.ts lines 23-62) contain no motion key. relay's token architecture (--rl-motion-duration-* consumed by motion.css) makes the override nearly free, yet a user on a system without the OS flag — or one who wants motion suppressed only in this app — has no recourse. This matters disproportionately because the web GUI runs in whatever browser the user has.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'reduceMotion' field (system/on/off) to THEME_SETTINGS in ui-theme/src/theme-settings.ts, and in appearance-apply.ts force the reduced duration tokens onto the root element when 'on' (mirroring what base.css's media query does), 'system' doing nothing beyond the existing media query. Cover with a ui-theme unit test in packages/client/ui-theme/tests/ asserting the applied token values per setting.
findings.title: prefers-reduced-motion is media-query-only; no user-facing reduce-motion override in Appearance

findings.detail: Lyra bundles Inter and JetBrains Mono latin variable subsets with unicode-range and a documented rationale (styles.css lines 21-56, ~86KB): system stacks 'render differently on every machine', which for a browser-served GUI is the normal case, not the edge case. relay-harness's type stack (packages/client/ui-theme/src/styles/base.css lines 54-57) resolves latin text from -apple-system / Segoe UI / Helvetica and code from SF Mono / Consolas / Menlo; the only shipped faces are local()-based 'Relay CJK' size-adjust aliases (base.css lines 19-51), which help CJK metrics but leave latin rendering platform-dependent. A user on Linux with none of those fonts gets a materially different chat UI than the one the Relay Focus design was drawn against. Lyra also ships Fira Code / Source Code Pro / IBM Plex Mono as selectable code faces (styles.css lines 66-105); relay's code stack is fixed.
findings.suggested_fix: Vendor the two latin variable woff2 files (Inter, JetBrains Mono via @fontsource-variable, same as Lyra) into ui-theme/src/assets, declared with font-display:swap and the latin unicode-range in base.css ahead of the system stack. Keep the existing 'Relay CJK' local() faces untouched — they solve a different (CJK metric) problem. Verify total added size stays near Lyra's ~86KB and that apps/web vendor chunking (vite.config.ts VENDOR_PACKAGES rule: font assets ride CSS) still caches well.
findings.title: Latin UI/code typefaces ride platform font stacks; Lyra self-hosts variable latin subsets

findings.detail: Lyra runs React 19.2.8, zustand 5.0.14, Vite 8.2.1 (Lyra packages/desktop/package.json devDependencies); relay-harness client pins react ^18.2.0 (ui-renderer, ui-primitives), zustand ~4.4.7 + immer ^10 (packages/client/runtime/package.json dependencies), vite ^6 (apps/web/package.json). The gap is real but already owned: .agents/notes/proposed/process/2026-08-23-staged-dependency-upgrades.md wave 3 sequences react+react-dom+types+plugin-react together with zustand 4→5 and use-sync-external-store removal (line 47), and line 78 warns that client code written during the staging period 'is written against the older API and may need revisiting'. Concretely still-18-shaped code that the wave will touch: ui-renderer's hand-rolled shim typings for use-sync-external-store/with-selector (packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/use-sync-external-store.d.ts) and its useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector bridge (bind.ts line 7), both removable once React 19 is in; and contract/store.ts's zustand/middleware + zustand/shallow imports whose import paths shift on zustand 5.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat this as execution of the existing proposed note rather than a new migration: (1) promote the wave-3 PR out of proposed/ before more Relay Focus client work lands; (2) in the same React 19 PR, delete use-sync-external-store.d.ts and switch bind.ts to the React-native store bridge, and fold contract/store.ts's zustand 4→5 import-path changes in (the note already couples them); (3) add the note's own acceptance criterion — the React PR updates both SDK expected outputs in the same PR per repo testing policy.
findings.title: Frontend stack majors (React 18 / zustand 4 / Vite 6) trail Lyra's (React 19 / zustand 5 / Vite 8) — planned, but migration debt accrues meanwhile

audits.summary: relay-harness's packages/client is already at or above Lyra's level on most axes Lyra is known for: seed-color theme derivation with contrast control (ui-theme derive.ts vs Lyra theme.ts), a motion token system honoring prefers-reduced-motion (ui-theme motion.css/base.css vs Lyra styles.css), frame-batched streaming publication (Notifier.markFrameDirty + PartialAccumulator vs Lyra coalesce.ts, including out-of-order flush protection via notifyNow), a projection-driven context-occupancy ring with per-segment breakdown (ContextMeter.tsx vs Lyra's context ring), and a large keyless Playwright e2e/snapshot suite in apps/web/tests. The remaining material gaps are capability- and process-shaped, not architecture-shaped: Lyra ships a CodeMirror-based syntax-highlighted file editor where relay renders a plain textarea, exposes a user-facing reduce-motion override and self-hosted latin variable fonts that relay lacks, and institutionalizes "measure the rendered app" verification (pixel hashes, computed-style probes) that relay's 100%-coverage + DOM-structural e2e gates do not replicate. Stack majors (React 19 / zustand 5 / Vite 8) trail but are already sequenced in a proposed dependency-upgrade note, so the actionable item is executing it before more React-18-shaped client code accrues.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a scripts gate (following existing convention: scripts/web-test-face.spec.ts) that asserts apps/web/tsconfig.json's exclude list is exactly the complement of tsconfig.host.json's apps/web/tests include entries and that the union covers every file in apps/web/tests/**; better, derive both lists from a single manifest (like scripts/doc-budgets.manifest.json) and dedupe chat-scroll-fixture.ts.
findings.detail: Whether an apps/web test file is checked in the host or client tsc program is decided by two hand-maintained lists: tsconfig.host.json includes each apps/web/tests file individually (lines 12-91, no glob), while apps/web/tsconfig.json excludes the same files one-by-one from its `include: ["src", "tests"]` glob (lines 24-110). A new web e2e test added to the vitest.web.config.ts glob (which runs it in CI) but not added to both lists either (a) silently lands in the CLIENT program via apps/web's `tests` glob — the wrong compiler face for host-plane Context merges — or (b) escapes typecheck entirely. There is no gate syncing the lists, and drift is already present: `apps/web/tests/chat-scroll-fixture.ts` appears twice in tsconfig.host.json (lines 26 and 82) and twice in apps/web/tsconfig.json's exclude. scripts/run-web-snapshots.ts:4-7 keeps a third parallel file list (serial owners) with the same failure mode.
findings.title: apps/web 测试文件由三份手工维护清单把关，新测试会进错编译面或完全逃过 typecheck

findings.suggested_fix: Widen the fallback workspace config to entry: tests/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}, tests/**/*.e2e.ts, tests/**/*.snapshot.ts and project: src/**/*.{ts,tsx}, tests/**/*.{ts,tsx}, then delete the now-redundant per-package overrides. knip --treat-config-hints-as-errors keeps this fails-loud.
findings.detail: The wildcard workspace `packages/*/*` declares entry [tests/**/*.spec.ts] and project [src/**/*.ts, tests/**/*.ts] (knip.json:246-254). All .tsx globs exist only in ~30 explicit per-package overrides; client packages without an override — verified missing: ui-user-questions (src/client/QuestionComposer.tsx), ui-session-tree (SessionTreeCanvas.tsx etc.), ui-titlebar, ui-git, ui-agents-panel, ui-surfaces, ui-files, ui-diff, ui-preview, ui-theme, ui-attachment, ui-reference, ui-brand-official, ui-memory-center, ui-sidebar — have their entire .tsx source and .tsx/.e2e/.snapshot test files invisible to knip: no unused-file, unused-export, or unused-dependency detection. New client packages silently get the same hole unless someone remembers a knip.json entry.
findings.title: knip 回退 workspace 配置不含 .tsx 与 e2e/snapshot 入口，15+ client 包的 .tsx 源码完全逃过 knip 检测

findings.suggested_fix: Either vendor the workflow definitions into this repo, or add a fails-loud presence check at the top of ci-workflow.spec.ts and the issue-management script that names the missing sibling checkout and which gates depend on it.
findings.detail: `pnpm run test:issue-management` executes `node ../.github/issue-management/policy.test.mjs` (package.json:41), and scripts/ci-workflow.spec.ts:7 hardcodes `resolve(root, '..')` to read `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The spec runs in the default unit lane (vitest.config.ts testIncludes includes `scripts/**/*.spec.ts`), and the gate is in ciSharedStaticGates/check-all (scripts/run-gates.ts:288,259), so a clean clone of relay-harness without the sibling checkout makes `pnpm run test`, `check:ci:static` and `check:all` fail with an opaque ENOENT. AGENTS.md never mentions this cross-repo requirement.
findings.title: CI 定义与 issue-management 门禁依赖仓库外的 ../.github 目录，独立 clone 会失败

findings.suggested_fix: Add a run-gates leaf (e.g. in ci-consumers after the exe build, or a dedicated aggregate) invoking test:python-carriers, or wire it into the python release/exe workflow where carriers are produced.
findings.detail: `RLH_REQUIRE_BUNDLED_CARRIERS=1` appears only in python/sdk/tests/test_bundled_runtime.py and python/development*.md; grep over ../.github finds no invocation of test:python-carriers, and ci.yml:363 runs plain `uv run ... pytest` without the flag. The bundled carriers are what the Python SDK distributes, so a rebuild that ships stale carriers passes CI; the check exists only as a documented manual command and in no run-gates aggregate.
findings.title: test:python-carriers（bundled carriers 校验）没有被任何 run-gates 聚合或 workflow 执行，CI 对 Python 载体漂移不设防

findings.suggested_fix: Compute the exclusions lazily/only when coverage instrumentation is active (e.g. key off the argv containing --coverage or an explicit env), and memoize; the probe's own comment already requires it to match the suites' hasPwsh resolution, so reuse the same resolve.ts path but gate the spawn.
findings.detail: `const pwshCoverageExclusions = spawnSync(resolvePwshPath(), ['-NoLogo', ...], ...)` is a top-level const consumed only by coverage.exclude, but vitest evaluates the whole config for `pnpm run test` too. On hosts with pwsh installed this launches a real PowerShell process (~100-500ms, serial) before any test starts; on pwsh-less hosts it pays a failed-spawn probe. It also couples the default test config to packages/shell/pwsh-local source at load time.
findings.title: vitest.config.ts 在每次配置加载时同步 spawn pwsh 探针，普通 `pnpm test` 也为 coverage-only 的排除清单买单

findings.suggested_fix: Extract a shared web-lane factory into vitest.shared.ts (test block + plugin list) that all three web configs consume, mirroring how vitestExecArgv/standardDecoratorPlugin are already shared.
findings.detail: vitest.config.ts, vitest.e2e.config.ts and vitest.snapshot.config.ts all set `setupFiles: ['./scripts/test-invariants.ts']` and pass `standardDecoratorPlugin()`; vitest.web.config.ts and vitest.web.perf.config.ts (via spread) set neither, and vitest.web-stress.config.ts also omits standardDecoratorPlugin (the only config without it). Consequences: the jsdom canvas stub (test-invariants.ts:25-31) and the RegistryService invariant-companion patch apply to every lane except the web lanes, so real compositions booted by web e2e/snapshot tests run without the package invariant assertions the repo treats as mandatory; and any decorator-bearing .tsx imported by a stress test would transpile everywhere except the stress lane. perf/stress also inherit the web config's .env load even though their comment says they are outside the CI gate.
findings.title: web 三条 vitest lane 漂移：缺 test-invariants setupFile，web-stress 还缺 standardDecoratorPlugin

findings.suggested_fix: Split the exemption: keep server-side extensions (tool-cordis, cordis-host-runner, cordis-client-runner) under the per-file gate and narrow the client-UI exemption to packages/extensions/ui-cordis/src/client/**, or record the group in the same GUI-debt manifest as the client exemptions so it can be tracked to zero.
findings.detail: The exclude list contains `packages/extensions/*/src/**/*.ts` and `**/*.tsx` (vitest.config.ts:266-267), so tool-cordis, cordis-host-runner, cordis-client-runner and ui-cordis have no per-file 100% enforcement at all, unlike every other non-client group. Unlike the adjacent client-file exemptions, this one is not annotated with a TODO(gui) or reason comment. AGENTS.md's 'test:coverage, not test, is the CI coverage gate' makes this a silent policy carve-out for a whole package group.
findings.title: packages/extensions/*/src 整组被排除在 per-file 100% 覆盖率门禁之外

findings.suggested_fix: Delete the redundant ignorePatterns/options duplication from .oxlintrc.staged.json (keep only extends + the intentional typeAware:false delta), or add a scripts spec pinning the staged config's effective ignores to a documented subset.
findings.detail: .oxlintrc.staged.json `extends` .oxlintrc.json, so the parent's ignorePatterns already apply; the child re-lists a subset and has already dropped `.claude/**`, `**/.oxlint-contract-*/**`, the ghostty adapter and the typert type-model fixture entries. If oxlint's extends merges ignores (current behavior), the whole block is dead weight that invites copy-edit drift; if it were ever treated as overriding, the omissions would silently widen the pre-commit lint (with --fix --stage_fixed, i.e. auto-rewriting staged files the full lint ignores).
findings.title: .oxlintrc.staged.json 手工复制主配置的 ignorePatterns，语义要么冗余要么已漂移

findings.suggested_fix: Move one shared positiveIntFromEnv(name, fallback) into vitest.shared.ts (or scripts/), and have run-gates/coverage-partitions/run-web-snapshots consume it; keep the per-call-site error message naming the variable.
findings.detail: The same parse-strict-positive-int-or-throw logic exists as positiveIntFromEnv in vitest.e2e.config.ts and vitest.snapshot.config.ts (identical bodies), concurrencyFromEnv and positiveIntArg in scripts/run-gates.ts, parseCoveragePartitionCount/coverageTestTimeoutArgs in scripts/coverage-partitions.ts, and an inline copy in scripts/run-web-snapshots.ts. Error messages and strictness (e.g. `String(parsed) === raw` vs Number.isInteger) already diverge subtly between copies, which is exactly the asymmetry the repo's duplication gate is meant to catch.
findings.title: 正整数环境变量解析逻辑在 5+ 处复制，行为约定开始分叉

files: .github/workflows（../.github，gen-third-party-notices 的 manifest 输入未全量匹配）
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the lefthook glob with patches/**, scripts/types/** and any other manifest-declared inputs, and add a scripts spec that asserts the glob covers gen-third-party-notices.ts's declared inputs.
findings.detail: The pre-commit job's glob covers package.json/pnpm-workspace.yaml/pnpm-lock.yaml/vendor/README.md/python pyproject/generator sources, but its own comment admits the deleted-manifest case 'falls through to the freshness assertion in the test lane'. Inputs outside the glob (e.g. patches/* added via pnpm-workspace patchedDependencies, or scripts/types/client-build-environment/index.d.ts referenced from knip entries) regenerate only when the test lane runs, which the AGENTS.md pre-push policy says should NOT default to the full suite — so a touched input can reach CI stale with no local signal.
findings.title: lefthook third-party-notices 触发 glob 与生成器实际读取的输入面不完全一致（自述缺口仅覆盖删除场景）

audits.summary: 仓库级构建/测试配置整体设计水平很高：run-gates.ts 的依赖图调度（validate → needs/after → skip 传播 → allowFailure）自洽且边界校验完整；coverage 门禁（per-file 100% + 分片 + 豁免重套件并行）与 vitest 六个配置的 source-plane 解析约定（tsconfig.base.json paths facade）一致。主要问题集中在三类：(1) 三份手工维护的文件清单（tsconfig.host.json 的 apps/web include、apps/web/tsconfig.json 的 exclude、run-web-snapshots 的 serialFiles）没有任何同步门禁，新增 web 测试会静默进错编译面或逃过 typecheck，且 chat-scroll-fixture 重复条目证明漂移已发生；(2) knip 回退 workspace 配置缺 .tsx/.e2e/.snapshot glob，使十余个 client 包的 tsx 源码完全脱离 knip 检测；(3) `test:python-carriers` 与 `../.github` 外部依赖分别构成未接线的门禁与移植性地雷。另有 web lane 间 setupFiles/装饰器插件的配置漂移，以及每次 `pnpm test` 都要付一次 pwsh spawnSync 探针的小额热路径成本。

findings.detail: Every searchSessions/searchEvents call runs _reconcile → _observeStable, which for EVERY live session calls observeLive → observeSession (src/index.ts:535, 856-870): structuredClone(header + all events), JSON.stringify of the complete log, then sha256. Nothing is cached between calls — even a fully unchanged corpus pays O(total live log bytes) clone+serialize per search request. For an active session with a multi-MB log this makes every search (e.g. a UI keystroke) re-serialize every live transcript. The structuredClone is pure waste here: the fingerprint only needs serialized bytes (JSON.stringify on the frozen originals would do), and the clone is discarded after buildSessionEventSearchDocuments consumes it.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the fingerprint from cheap change markers instead of log bytes (e.g. session.seq + header + a per-session mutation counter exposed by Session), or cache the observation keyed by (sessionId, seq, header) and only re-serialize when the watermark moves; drop the structuredClone in observeSession since the input is already immutable.
findings.title: SQLite session-query re-fingerprints every live session's full log on every search

findings.detail: corpus.ts:98 resolves one session by calling listPersisted(persistence) — a full backend list — and only then inspectPersisted. Every readSession/readEvent/listEvents/readTitle/filterEvents/readSurface on a persisted session therefore pays a whole-root walk. On the JSONL backend list() = listArtifacts (src/index.ts:472-509), which per session directory does 2 open()-based exists() probes, a first-line read (zstd: frame scan + decompress) plus assertStoredIdentity with two realpath calls (src/index.ts:808-848). Reading one log against a store with thousands of sessions costs thousands of file operations; findLog(id) (src/index.ts:774-795) already implements the direct O(project dirs) resolution, and inspect() alone distinguishes not-found.
findings.suggested_fix: In SessionCorpus.load, drop the listing: call inspectPersisted directly and map its not-found error to SESSION_QUERY_SESSION_NOT_FOUND (the live re-check after inspect already exists); or add an id-addressed existence hook to the persistence seam for the pre-check.
findings.title: SessionCorpus.load lists the entire persisted corpus to resolve a single session id

findings.detail: session-persistence-sqlite (schema.ts:121-133) and session-query-sqlite (schema.ts:55-67) both refuse a database they do not own (application_id check, unversioned-with-objects check, recognized-table check). storage-sqlite has neither: configureDatabase only compares user_version, then CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS units/unit_globals and stamps user_version = 1 when it was 0 (schema.ts:82-107). Consequences: (a) pointing the configured path at an arbitrary foreign SQLite file with user_version=0 silently adopts it, creates its tables alongside unknown ones, and stamps it as a Relay storage DB; (b) a foreign file that happens to have user_version=1 is accepted with no validation at all, and failures surface only later as per-statement errors. This contradicts AGENTS.md 'Misconfiguration fails loud' and the sibling backends' explicit ownership protocol.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the sibling protocol: stamp a STORAGE_SQLITE_APPLICATION_ID via PRAGMA application_id, reject application_id≠0∧≠ours and application_id=0 with existing user tables at open, and validate the expected object set before stamping.
findings.title: storage-sqlite silently adopts foreign SQLite databases (no application_id, no ownership rejection)

findings.detail: The shipped json backend persists session_projcache beside workspace.json. The cache service checkpoints on every turn/end of every session (src/index.ts:205-209); each write structuredClones all projection states and puts one record. JsonKvUnit.putRecord publishes by rewriting the COMPLETE unit file (serialize all tables + fsync + directory fsync, storage-json/src/unit.ts:133-140, atomic.ts:24-40). With S sessions in the cache, every turn end in any session rewrites O(total cache bytes), and one session's growth makes every other session's checkpoint more expensive — quadratic write amplification on a per-turn hot path, with projection states serialized twice per write (checkpoint() clone + snapshotJsonValue in put()).
findings.suggested_fix: Ship session_projcache on the sqlite backend by default (the JSON unit cannot amortize per-record writes), and skip the intermediate structuredClone in checkpoint() by making snapshotJsonValue the single serialization pass.
findings.title: Projection-cache checkpoint on JSON backend rewrites the whole store on every turn/end

findings.detail: session-persistence-sqlite/src/sql.ts:39 and schema.ts:210 hard-code a per-version statement resource set-user-version-17 alongside the SCHEMA_VERSION=17 constant (schema.ts:19). Bumping SCHEMA_VERSION without adding a matching set-user-version-NN resource makes initializeDatabase stamp the OLD version, so every fresh database is created unopenable (the next open refuses its own stamp). Nothing mechanically ties the resource name, the SQL_RESOURCES list entry, and the constant together; the existing sql-resource-boundary test checks only the closed resource list, not version agreement.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the per-version resource with a build-owned interpolated statement (`PRAGMA user_version = ' + SCHEMA_VERSION` from the single constant — safe since it is a compile-time integer), or add a gate asserting the resource name suffix equals SCHEMA_VERSION.
findings.title: SCHEMA_VERSION bump touches three unsynchronized places and can self-stamp a stale version

findings.detail: schema.ts:31-35 says the open sequence 'deliberately mirrors the session-persistence-sqlite / session-query-sqlite open sequence', but the shared pieces stop at mkdir/createDatabaseFile/journal_mode: the sibling sequences' ownership validation, trusted_schema=0, mmap_size=0, and synchronous=FULL checks are all absent. A reader (and the duplication gate) is told the sequences agree when they diverge exactly on the safety-critical parts; this is also what allowed finding 3 to ship.
findings.suggested_fix: Either complete the mirror (preferred — fixes finding 3) or rewrite the comment to name exactly which steps are shared and list the omitted hardening as a deliberate difference with its reason.
findings.title: storage-sqlite jscpd comment claims to 'deliberately mirror' the sibling open sequences it omits

findings.detail: The SQLite packed-row path bounds decompression (decodeData passes maxOutputLength = MAX_PACKED_DATA_BYTES, compression.ts:108-114), but the JSONL backend decompresses without any output bound: decompressZstdFrame (zstd.ts:120-122), decompressZstdPrefix (zstd.ts:154-156), and the multi-frame decoder's plaintexts are all fed straight from on-disk bytes. A corrupted or tampered log (a durable/file boundary that AGENTS.md says must be validated) can declare an arbitrarily large frame content size and force Node's zstdDecompress to allocate it during load/list — readFirstZstdLine (src/index.ts:758) and readPrefix both exercise this on corruption-controlled input.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass a sane maxOutputLength (e.g. the packed-row 1 MiB bound for event frames, a header-sized bound in readFirstZstdLine) so oversized expansions fail as a corrupt session log instead of allocating.
findings.title: JSONL zstd read paths decompress with no maxOutputLength bound

findings.detail: The dispose effect drains via `while (this.chains.size > 0) await Promise.allSettled([...this.chains.values()])` with no timeout. SQLiteSessionPersistence accepts busyTimeoutMs up to MAX_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_147_483_647 (session-persistence-sqlite/src/index.ts:33,61), so a contended database can keep an appendBatch in begin-immediate retry for weeks while app teardown waits on the drain loop, with no diagnostic naming the stuck session/operation. The same shape applies to a hung fsync on the JSONL side.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the drain with a configured (or at least logged) deadline that names which session id's chain never settled, so teardown fails loud instead of hanging; keep durability by rethrowing rather than silently abandoning buffered events.
findings.title: PersistenceCoordinator dispose drain loop has no deadline against a stalled backend write

findings.detail: listArtifacts parses headers via parseHeaderMeta (format.ts:404-413), which runs isHeaderLine/fromHeaderLine but never refuseForeignFormatVersion — the guard the read path deliberately applies BEFORE shape validation (format.ts:240-247) so users see 'upgrade the harness'.
