A session written by a newer harness at a version that still satisfies today's header shape (or an older retired version) is returned by list()/listSnapshots() and surfaces in pickers and the session-query corpus with no marker; the refusal (with the upgrade text and raw-log path) appears only later at open time. The two read paths of the same format-version invariant are asymmetric.
findings.suggested_fix: Give parseHeaderMeta the same pre-shape version check (returning a typed 'unsupported version' marker instead of a header), and let list()/SessionCorpus expose it so pickers can show the upgrade hint instead of a silently unopenable row.
findings.title: list()/parseHeaderMeta skips the format-version refusal, so pickers surface sessions this build cannot open

findings.detail: storage-sqlite tests only cover version-mismatch rejection (tests/sqlite-backend.spec.ts:78,143). Nothing proves the open path rejects an unrelated SQLite file — the failure mode findings 3/6 describe, and the property both sibling backends test for. Once ownership validation is added, the acceptance path must prove each invalid case is rejected per AGENTS.md's mechanically-checkable-invariant rule. New cases belong in packages/storage/storage-sqlite/tests/sqlite-backend.spec.ts following the existing <name>.spec.ts convention.
findings.suggested_fix: Add cases to packages/storage/storage-sqlite/tests/sqlite-backend.spec.ts: a foreign database with foreign tables and user_version=0, a foreign application_id, and (after the fix) a same-application_id/wrong-object-set database — each asserted to reject with the ownership error before any table is created.
findings.title: No test that storage-sqlite rejects a foreign/unrelated database

findings.detail: _observeStable materializes documents for every non-shadowed persisted session whose revision differs from the index and rewrites all rows in one transaction (src/index.ts:497-516, 439-474). After a backend swap (JSONL → SQLite) or first index creation against a large store, a single search blocks on re-indexing the entire corpus with no bound, and the persistenceBinding change also bumps the epoch so all persisted cursors go stale. The behavior is arguably correct (the index must be complete before ranking) but nothing pins it, so a future incremental-index change could silently serve partial results. The spec belongs in packages/session-query/session-query-sqlite/tests/sqlite.spec.ts next to the existing reconcile coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a spec asserting that after mounting the engine against a pre-populated store the first search returns hits from ALL sessions (full reconciliation before the first page), and that a second search over an unchanged corpus performs no persisted inspect() calls (spy on persistence.inspect) — the regression guard for the finding-1 optimization work.
findings.title: session-query-sqlite: no test pins reconciliation behavior when the persistence backend identity changes

audits.summary: The session/storage/spill slice is unusually well-engineered: the persistence coordinator's per-id serialization, revision-gated preparation cache, write-behind batching, and crash-repair sequencing (torn-tail truncation, synthetic closers, seq-gap semantics) are correct and thoroughly tested, and the SQLite session backend's schema-ownership protocol (application_id, SCHEMA_VERSION revalidation, synchronous=FULL) matches the documented invariants. The verified defects cluster in three places: (1) hot-path efficiency — the SQLite session-query engine re-fingerprints every live session's entire log on every search, SessionCorpus.load walks the whole persisted corpus to read one session, and the projection-cache on the JSON storage backend rewrites the entire unit file per turn/end; (2) an asymmetry where storage-sqlite lacks the ownership validation its two sibling SQLite backends implement, silently adopting foreign databases; (3) maintenance friction around SCHEMA_VERSION pinned in three unsynchronized places. No data-loss or replay-correctness bug was found in the audited recovery paths.

findings.detail: frame-queue.ts:13-27 的 FrameQueue.push 无任何上限，也没有水位/丢帧/断开策略；api-proxy.ts:620-624 的 broadcast 把每个 session/event（含高频 assistant 增量、tool 事件）无条件 push 到每个 mux 订阅者的队列，sseResponse（fetch/handler.ts:203-236）的 enqueue 也不读 desiredSize。一个已连接但停读的 SSE 消费者（TCP 零窗口、被挂起的代理链路）会让该订阅者 buffer 无限增长；muxQueues 中的死队列也不会被清理。另外 drain 用 buffer.shift()（frame-queue.ts:47），大 buffer 下是 O(n²)。最近的 "bound sdk queues" 提交收敛了 SDK 方向，这是 host→浏览器方向剩下的最后一个无界队列，且 apiproxy README 的 Known Limitations 未提及。
findings.suggested_fix: 给 FrameQueue 加帧数或字节上限并定义慢消费者策略（超限即 end() 断开该订阅者，客户端已有重连+baseline 重放路径，语义安全）；drain 改用头指针代替 shift()；把上限写进 README Known Limitations 或做成 Config 字段。
findings.title: FrameQueue 每个 SSE 订阅者的缓冲完全无界，慢消费者可拖垮 host 内存

findings.detail: api-proxy.ts:1142-1153 对每批 16 个 cold session 用 Promise.allSettled，但只要任意一个 reject 就 throw 第一个 failure，整个 session.list 以 500 失败。一个损坏或半写的历史 artifact（掉电、后端 bug）会让浏览器的会话列表永久打不开，直到手工删除该 session。这与同文件对 projection 的取向相反：listProjectionsFor（api-proxy.ts:293-303）明确 fail-soft "a listing without projections is degraded, never broken"；README Known Limitations 也声明冷路径 "degrade only toward visibility"。逐行丢弃+计一条 warning 更符合已声明的失败方向。
findings.suggested_fix: 改为对该行降级（跳过并在 ctx.logger.warn 记录 sessionId 与原因），或至少聚合全部失败后按行降级、仅在全部失败时抛错；若坚持 fail-loud，在 README Known Limitations 写明该方向。
findings.title: session.list 冷摘要批次一票否决：单个坏冷日志让整个列表 500

findings.detail: usageView（memory-center/src/index.ts:441-489）对 workspace 内每个 persisted session 调 sessionQuery.readSession 拉全量事件数组并遍历 context/prepared 事件聚合 why-used；它被 list 的两个分支（:109、:124）和 read（:179）调用，即 Memory Center 每翻一页、每打开一条详情都做一次 O(全语料日志字节) 的扫描与解析。已有 SQLite 全文/事件索引的 session-query 包存在，却没有按 memory id 的定点查询路径。包内有 usageConcurrency=4 的并发限制，但总代价仍是全语料线性。
findings.suggested_fix: 在 session-query 增加按 evidence/evidenceId 的定点检索（索引 context/prepared contributions），usageView 只查命中的 session；短期先把扫描成本与语料规模的关系写进 memory-center README 的 Known Limitations。
findings.title: memory-center usageView 每次 list/read 全语料扫描所有 session 日志

findings.detail: README.md:78 写 "the table in `src/api-proxy.ts` handles questions only and has no approval entries"，但代码已有 pendingApprovals 注册表：api-proxy.ts:478（声明）、754-836（approval/request 监听、abort 竞态处理、replay baseline）、3103-3113（respond 分发）。README 甚至在同段说 wire 是 POST /api/respond + RpcReceipt——正是 approval 的应答通道。该行是 approval 通道落地前的旧文。
findings.suggested_fix: 改写该条为：questions 与 approvals 共享 /api/respond 的 rpcId 路由，pending 表在断连重连时以稳定 rpcId 重放 requested 帧；删除 "handles questions only" 的过时断言。
findings.title: apiproxy README Known Limitations 声称无 approval 表，与实现相悖（stale doc）

findings.detail: events.mux 每个订阅者安装 1 个广播 queue + 4-6 个 ctx.on/jobs 监听（api-proxy.ts:2877-2935），events.host 同样（:2949-3039），cleanup 依赖 queue.iterate 的 finally。现有测试（fetch-carrier.spec.ts、client-handler.spec.ts 等）验证帧内容，但没有任何测试验证：客户端 abort 后 generator 收尾、muxQueues 移除、session/event 监听器被 dispose。按 AGENTS.md "Registry contributions prove disposal"（HMR-safety 纪律），这个每客户端一段监听器的注册是最需要证明清理的路径之一；一旦 cleanup 失效，每个断开的标签页都会让所有后续 session 事件多推送一份并常驻内存。
findings.suggested_fix: 新增 packages/host/apiproxy/tests/api-proxy-mux.spec.ts：用真实 createApiProxy（非 fakeApi）开 mux 流，abort req.signal，断言 1) 生成器结束、2) 之后 append 的 session 事件不再产生帧、3) 反复开关 N 个流后监听器数量不增长（可通过再开一个流观察事件只收到一份来旁证）。
findings.title: mux/host 流订阅者清理（disposer 释放）无直接测试

findings.detail: prompt 的 admit() 把非 AttachmentError 的一切异常映射为 code:'agent-busy', message:'prompt rejected', details:{reason:String(error)}（api-proxy.ts:1903-1915）。carrier 层的约定是 "impl never throws business errors; reaching here means the implementation itself crashed"（fetch/handler.ts:186-191，返回 500），而这里把实现崩溃降级成一个暗示"稍后重试"的业务码，且 String(error) 可把内部堆栈/路径文本放进 wire details——与同文件其他域（如 subagentPromptError 统一返回 'internal' + 固定文案，api-proxy.ts:374）的做法不一致。
findings.suggested_fix: 收窄 catch：只有 steer/followup 的已知拒绝（inbox 满等，若存在类型化错误）映射 agent-busy；durablePromptContent 的 AttachmentError 保持现状；其余抛回 carrier 层让它走 500，或统一映射 code:'internal' 且不带原始错误文本。
findings.title: session.prompt 把所有内部异常吞成 agent-busy 并把原始错误串放进 wire details

findings.detail: mcp-servers/src/index.ts:209-248 在 host 侧手写解析 mcp-client 的 config（serverName/transport/command/args/env/cwd/url/headers/startupTimeoutMs），判断依据是 moduleName === 常量 || endsWith('mcp-client')（:210-211）。mcp-client 插件若新增配置字段或更名，Center 的组合来源行会静默少显示或误判来源（endsWith 启发式会把任何 *mcp-client 包都当 MCP 客户端行读）。这是同一配置格式的第二个解析点，违反 "one home per fact"。
findings.suggested_fix: 由 rlh-mcp-client 导出其 Config 的 zod schema 与 spec 投影函数（或 isMcpClientModule 判定），host 侧复用；至少把 endsWith 启发式换成 mcp-client 导出的显式判定。
findings.title: mcp-servers 网关手写复刻 mcp-client 配置投影与宽松命名启发式

findings.detail: updateQueue 对 action.kind==='steer' 强制 target==='next-turn' 且 agent.status==='running'，否则返回 steer-unavailable（api-proxy.ts:2005-2011）；而 prompt 的 mode:'steer' 路径（:1901，直调 agent.steer → agent-loop agent.ts:185-187 入 next-step 队列）不检查运行状态：对空闲 session 发 steer 会静默变成下轮的 next-step 上下文（queueItems 里仍渲染为 'steering' 气泡）。同一"steering 只属于进行中的 turn"决策被两个入口执行，一个拒绝、一个降级，客户端无法获得一致反馈。
findings.suggested_fix: 在 prompt 的 steer 分支加与 updateQueue 相同的检查（agent.status !== 'running' 时返回 steer-unavailable），或反之让 updateQueue 也接受降级语义；二选一并写进两侧 JSDoc。
findings.title: session.prompt 的 mode:'steer' 不强制 updateQueue 同款 running-turn 检查

findings.detail: hostOpenPathRequestSchema 只要求 path 非空（api/host.schema.ts:68-71），实现注释明确 "caller owns resolution"（native-path-opener.ts:177）。同组 browse 后端为同一类 wire 路径值专门建了 fullyQualified 栅栏，理由写在 JSDoc："a wire value must never resolve against the host cwd"（directory-picker/src/index.ts:82-84、directory-picker-browse/src/index.ts:113-117、316）。openPath 是同一 wire 上的同构值，却允许 '\\foo'、'foo/bar' 之类值在 host 进程 cwd（或 Windows 当前盘）语境下被 xdg-open/open/PowerShell 消费。
findings.suggested_fix: 在 host.openPath/openDocument 的 schema 或 api-proxy 入口复用 fullyQualified 检查（拒绝非完全限定路径并返回 bad-request），与 browse/list、createDirectory 的既有栅栏对齐。
findings.title: host.openPath 的 wire schema 接受任意非空字符串，相对路径会落到 host 进程 cwd

findings.detail: viewFor 在 presenter 抛错或参数不可解析时用 console.error（history-views.ts:68），而同包的 listProjectionsFor/subagentHistoryProjections 都走 ctx.logger.warn（api-proxy.ts:300、332）。该路径在每个 mux 订阅者的每条 session/event 上运行，一处坏 presenter 会在高吞吐事件流上向 stdout 刷屏，绕过 Host 日志的级别/汇聚管线；webserver 包甚至明确立规 "This package never prints"。fetch/client.ts:286、401 的 console 在浏览器侧可接受，但 history-views 拿得到 ctx，没有理由。
findings.suggested_fix: viewFor 已持有 ctx，改用 ctx.logger.warn 并保留 "falling back to generic" 语义；可加每会话去重避免事件风暴下刷屏。
findings.title: history-views 用 console.error 输出 presenter 失败，绕过 ctx.logger

audits.summary: host 组（packages/host，~12.6k 行 src）以 apiproxy（8.9k 行）为核心：fetch/SSE carrier、zod 双层解析、approval/question 待答表、session 生命周期去重链（sessionCreations/presetSwitches/workspaceCreationChain）和导出 ZIP 的 durability barrier 都实现严谨，进程/worker 边界（win32 dialog 子进程、native-command 无 shell 调用、skill ZIP 导入的压缩炸弹/路径栅栏）校验完整。最近两次提交覆盖的 sdk 队列与 fencing 没有明显遗漏，但 host→浏览器方向的 FrameQueue 仍是完全无界队列（唯一的高优先级问题），另有 memory-center 每次读都全语料扫描 session 日志的性能问题、一条与代码相悖的 stale README，以及若干 enforcement 不对称。webserver 的 DNS-rebinding 栅栏实际位于 client/connection 节点半（trustedHosts，403），host 侧 415 JSON fence 与之配合，无缺口。

findings.detail: The authoritative `window.shell` Electron preload API is re-declared as a partial local interface in 10 packages, each naming it differently and each with its own null-safe accessor: ui-settings-general/src/client/desktop-shell.ts:85-112 (DesktopShell + desktopShell() + canPersistCloseBehavior), ui-settings-remote/src/client/desktop-shell.ts:41-83 (a second DesktopShell with different members + desktopShell() + hasRemoteApi), ui-surfaces/src/client/apply.ts:87-109 (third DesktopShell + readWindowShell()), ui-product-shell/src/client/mode.ts:12-24 (DesktopModeShell), ui-preview/src/client/shell.ts:265 (PreviewShell), ui-files/src/client/shell.ts:101 and FilePreview.tsx:109 (FilesShell / DesktopPreviewShell), ui-user-terminal/src/client/shell.ts:43 and apply.ts:74 (PtyShell / inline openExternal), ui-diff/src/client/shell.ts:96 (DiffShell), ui-git/src/client/apply.ts:68 (GitShell). Two packages even use the same exported name `DesktopShell` for disjoint member sets. Any rename or signature change in the Electron preload silently desyncs each copy; there is no single place that states what `window.shell` is.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare one canonical `DesktopShellBridge` contract (all optional IPC members) plus one `desktopShell()` accessor in rlh-client-runtime (React-free, so it fits the object layer and the client bundle purity gate), and have each package narrow to the subset it uses via `Pick<...>`. Update the Electron preload to satisfy that interface so drift becomes a compile error.
findings.title: Electron `window.shell` bridge hand-declared 11 times across 10 client packages

findings.detail: ui-agent-preset/src/client/settings-store.ts:38-49 persists the default preset via `api.settings.update({ ns, patch: { default: id } })` with no `expectedRevision`, even though the wire field exists (packages/host/apiproxy/src/api/settings.schema.ts:48-52) and every sibling settings writer fences on it: SettingsScopeController.write (ui-settings/src/client/settings-scope.ts:124-151), PermissionPresetSettingsController.select (ui-permission-presets/src/client/settings-store.ts:142-152), and the Models editors (ui-settings-models/src/client/ProviderEditor.tsx:307, CustomProviderCard.tsx:146-152, VisionModelPicker.tsx:139 — the latter even carries a user-facing conflict string in locales). Two concurrent writers (two windows, or the General row racing the management section) can silently last-write-win the default preset. The response view is also dropped instead of folded via `describeFace.acceptView`, leaving the shared mirror stale until the next `settings/document-updated` push.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the agent-presets namespace revision from the shared mirror (like PermissionPresetSettingsController does), pass `expectedRevision`, and fold the returned namespace view back with `describeFace.acceptView` so a conflict surfaces as a retriable error instead of a silent overwrite.
findings.title: Agent-preset default write bypasses settings revision fencing used by every other settings writer

findings.detail: connection/src/client/index.ts:9 statically imports `./fixture.ts` (3,335 lines, ~150KB source of mock transcripts/API data) and only branches on it at runtime (`const fixture = ... URLSearchParams(...).has('fixture')`, line 88-90). Because the branch is a runtime condition, no bundler can drop `FixtureApiClient` or its data from the production web bundle; the entire fixture dataset ships to every browser solely to support a dev query param.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the fixture transport behind a dynamic `await import('./fixture.ts')` resolved only when the query param is present (boot is already async-friendly via the top-level plugin apply), or move FixtureApiClient behind the existing `__RLH_BOOT_GATE__` dev seam so tsdown tree-shakes it out of the product bundle.
findings.title: Test fixture transport (3,335 lines / ~150KB) statically imported into the production client bundle

findings.detail: connection/src/index.ts:151 runs the capacity assertion only `if (ctx.get('apiProxy') !== undefined)`, and the deferred re-check inside `ctx.inject(['apiProxy'], ...)` (line 184) reads `ctx.get('attachments')` at that moment; neither re-runs when the attachments plugin registers later. If the composition loads client-connection before rlh-attachment (or attachments is absent at that phase), a `maxRequestBodyBytes` below the required image envelope is silently accepted and the failure only appears later as runtime 413s on aggregate image sends — the exact 'silently skip a missing referent' AGENTS.md forbids.
findings.suggested_fix: Register a deferred assertion that re-runs when `attachments` appears (e.g. `ctx.inject(['attachments'], ...)` alongside the apiProxy injection), or make the capacity check unconditional by declaring the minimum required envelope independently of the optional service and validating config against that constant.
findings.title: client-connection body-capacity assertion silently skipped when attachments registers late

findings.detail: ContextInspectorAction.tsx renders `Context {count}` as the visible button text (line 18), `truncated` as a Pill (line 46), and `context/prepared #{trace.seq}` (line 32) as literals, while the same component registers zh/en dictionaries and consumes `t('open')`, `t('title')` etc. The Chinese UI therefore shows untranslated English in the header action. The local `format()` helper (lines 9-11) also re-implements the `{name}` template interpolation the locale translate seat already provides, so two interpolation implementations coexist in one file.
findings.suggested_fix: Add keys (e.g. `badge`, `truncated`, `trace.source`) to both dictionaries in locales.ts, render through `t(...)`, and drop the local `format()` in favor of `t(key, params)`.
findings.title: Context Inspector renders hardcoded English labels outside the locale system it registers

findings.detail: Client AGENTS.md export-discipline rule 1 says implementation components, constants, and controllers stay internal, and rule 2 says same-package tests import `../src/client/...` directly ('never widen the public API to make a test compile'). Verified consumers show these /client value exports are used only by their own package's tests: ContextInspectorAction (ui-context-inspector/src/client/index.ts:9), CodeIndexCenterSection + CodeIndexCenterStore (ui-code-index-center/src/client/index.ts:11-12), MessageEditAction (ui-message-edit/src/client/index.ts:20), MemoryCenterStore (ui-memory-center/src/client/index.ts:13), writeDefaultPreset + AGENT_PRESET_SETTINGS_NS (ui-agent-preset/src/client/index.ts:46), ModelDirectory + ModelDirectoryResolver (ui-model-selection/src/client/index.ts:29-31), GoalBar + GoalDock (ui-goal/src/client/index.ts:26), CommandDirectory + CommandUiRuntime (ui-commands/src/client/index.ts:20-21), SettingsDocumentStore (ui-settings-general/src/client/index.ts:51). knip does not flag entrypoint exports, so this drift persists.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the value exports (keep type exports) from the /client entries and switch the corresponding specs to direct `../src/client/*.ts` imports, per the stated rule; consider a `verify-client-packages` check that any `/client` value export has a consumer outside its own package.
findings.title: ui-* /client entrypoints value-export implementation components and controllers with zero external consumers

findings.detail: mode.ts:53 and :73 obtain the generated productMode Remote via `(this.ctx.remote as unknown as { productMode: ProductModeRemote }).productMode`, where ProductModeRemote is a local hand-typed `{ get(); set(request) }` interface (lines 12-17). The host-generated face for the same remote already exists in api-remotes (ProductMode is imported from there at line 4); the double cast hides any wire-shape change from the compiler at exactly the boundary (browser↔host RPC) where the repo mandates typed contracts.
findings.suggested_fix: Type the remote against the generated api-remotes client face for productMode (the same pattern ui-memory-center/store.ts uses with `ctx.remote.memoryCenter`), deleting the local ProductModeRemote interface and both `as unknown as` casts.
findings.title: ui-product-shell re-declares the productMode remote interface behind a double cast

findings.detail: ui-jobs/src/client/locales.ts owns the `job` namespace status strings ('status.running', 'status.stopping', ...). ui-agents-panel/src/client/locales.ts re-declares the same five concepts as its own `jobs.status.*` keys (AgentsPanel.tsx:20-24 maps them) so the same host states have two copy sources that must be edited in lockstep in both languages. Separately, the exact `messageOf` helper is duplicated verbatim in ui-settings-models/src/client/store.ts:59-61 and ui-agent-preset/src/client/settings-store.ts:20-25, and the inline `error instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)` pattern appears in ~28 files across the slice — a shared coercion util in rlh-client-runtime would delete all of them.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the five job-status keys into the shared `common` vocabulary (or have the agents panel render entries through the `job` namespace it already can bind), and add `messageOf(error)` to rlh-client-runtime for the settings/model consumers.
findings.title: Duplicated job-status copy and error-message coercion across settings-adjacent packages

findings.detail: store.ts:11-12 keeps `pages: Map<string, MemoryCenterSnapshot>` and `details: Map<string, MemoryCenterDetail>` as plugin-lifetime state (the store is constructed once in apply, ui-memory-center/src/client/index.ts:27). Keys are full request JSON (line 24) including free-text search queries, so each distinct search term or filter combination permanently retains a full snapshot page until a governance write or `connection/reset` clears it (invalidate, line 117-122). A long browsing/search-heavy session grows without bound in the browser tab.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the cache (small LRU, e.g. last N pages/details) or drop entries by workspace/session when the selection changes; the existing generation guard already keeps correctness intact while trimming.
findings.title: MemoryCenterStore caches are unbounded for the whole browser session

findings.description: Group package table is stale: 20 shipped ui-* plugins are unlisted and one row points at a directory that does not exist

All 20 missing packages do have their own READMEs; only the group index is stale.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the 20 rows to both language tables and rename the row anchor to `ui-permission-presets/`; consider a gate script comparing the client table against directory listings (the repo already freshness-gates generated docs elsewhere).
findings.title: packages/client README table missing 20 ui-* packages and links to non-existent ui-permission/

findings.detail: connection/src/client/connection.ts:3-4 states 'Reconnect/backoff tunables (deployment-varying — no hardcoded tunables; these become the future ctx.connection plugin's Config)' with CONNECTION_DEFAULTS (lines 18-23: 500ms base, x2 factor, 10s cap, 3s stream-open timeout). The providing plugin (connection/src/client/index.ts:86-153) takes no Config at all, so the values are fixed constants reachable only programmatically through `start(sinks, config)` — the exact 'DEFAULT_* constant is not configurability' shape AGENTS.md prohibits for deployment-varying choices.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a validated `ConnectionConfig` (schemastery, mirroring ConnectionConfig fields) to the client connection plugin and thread its resolved defaults into `start()` when the runtime does not override them; then remove the deferral comment.
findings.title: Connection reconnect/backoff tunables are constructor options, not a validated plugin Config

findings.detail: history.ts:14-41 loops `sessions.history` in 100-message pages, `pages.unshift(page.events)` per round, and returns `pages.flat()` — the complete session log is materialized in the browser with no byte/message ceiling and no early stop. For a long-lived session (tens of thousands of entries, tool payloads included) this is a large one-shot allocation and wire transfer triggered by opening the tree, and it re-runs from seq 0 on every open since nothing caches or caps the read.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap the tree read at the newest K pages with an explicit 'older history not loaded' marker (the canvas only needs the lineage head), or stream pages into the model incrementally so cancelation via the existing `signal` can stop mid-read without discarding work.
findings.title: Session tree reads the complete session log into memory with no cap

audits.summary: The audited client slice (ui-settings family, ~40 small ui-* packages, and packages/client/connection) is generally high quality: stores use generation guards, single-flight mirrors, and revision-fenced writes consistently, and JSDoc contracts are unusually thorough. The dominant problem is cross-package duplication of hand-rolled boundary contracts — most notably 11 separate partial declarations of the Electron `window.shell` preload bridge across 10 packages, plus duplicated locale copy and error-coercion helpers — which is exactly the "unexplained asymmetry / missed extraction" smell AGENTS.md flags and which blocks the frontend↔backend wiring goal by making the desktop IPC surface unverifiable in one place. Two correctness issues stand out: ui-agent-preset writes the settings document without the revision fencing every sibling writer uses, and the production client bundle statically ships a 150KB test-fixture transport. Doc drift in the group README (20 unlisted packages, one broken directory reference) is the main doc gap; test coverage is dense (CI gates 100% per-file) so no material test gaps were verified.

findings.detail: InputMachine implements `set-invalid` (machine.ts:176, onSetInvalid at :366-376), InputEvent declares it (input/contract.ts:260), Occurrence carries `invalid` (input/contract.ts:176), and decorations render the bit (input/decorations.ts:29,125) — but nothing can ever produce it. Repo-wide grep shows the only references are the contract, the machine, and tests/input-machine.client.spec.ts. InputHub wires exactly four scoped listeners (input/hub.ts:100-110: begin-command, insert-reference, consume-token, insert-text) and SessionInputShell exposes no setInvalid verb, so a reference whose owner fails to resolve can never render invalid and the documented 'Owner-resolution result' behavior is unreachable.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire the path (a scoped `slash/input-set-invalid`-style listener plus a shell verb) or delete the event, handler, `Occurrence.invalid`, and the decoration branch together, updating input/contract.ts JSDoc — the pre-release stance allows removing unowned paths outright.
findings.title: InputEvent 'set-invalid' and the Occurrence.invalid styling bit are unreachable in production

findings.detail: InputHub routes `slash/input-consume-token` to shell.consumeToken (hub.ts:106), which re-implements the guard-and-splice itself via setDraft (facade.ts:340-351) instead of dispatching the machine's `consume-token` event. The machine handler (machine.ts:333-359) is therefore exercised only by tests/input-machine.client.spec.ts. The two implementations already diverge: the machine's span branch runs casOk (draftRev AND bounds sanity, machine.ts:280-283), while facade.consumeToken checks only `span.draftRev !== snapshot.draftRev` before splicing. Both clear `paste` and push an undo unit today, so the parity is equivalent — but any future edit to one copy silently desynchronizes the undo/paste/claim side effects, and the duplication itself is what AGENTS.md's 'unexplained asymmetry' rule flags.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the facade dispatch the machine's `consume-token` event and read the draftRev advance for its boolean return (the machine JSDoc already defines this contract), or delete onConsumeToken from the machine and move its JSDoc contract onto the facade copy — one owner, not two.
findings.title: Machine 'consume-token' handler is test-only; facade re-implements the same CAS splice over setDraft (two drifting implementations)

findings.detail: ComposerBlocks.forget is documented as 'The session scope's disposer calls this' (input/blocks.ts:46-49), but repo-wide grep finds zero callers (only unrelated longTermMemory.forget hits). apply.ts constructs the registry but never hooks a session-scope effect to drop stores. Consequences: (1) `stores` grows one SnapshotStore per session ever materialized for the app lifetime — the unbounded-growth class the audit priorities call out; (2) if a session id is re-materialized after teardown, the composer silently inherits the old session's block. The composer-bar inject (apply.ts:287) creates stores on first read, so the map is populated for every session the user visits.
findings.suggested_fix: Register the teardown in InputHub.shellFor's existing scope effect (hub.ts:100-119 already runs at scope disposal): call composerBlocks.forget(id) there, and add a HMR-safety test asserting the store is dropped after scope disposal.
findings.title: ComposerBlockRegistry.forget is never called; per-session block stores accumulate for the app lifetime

findings.detail: When the draft is empty but images are attached, facade.submit sends outside the machine: `void this.deps.defaultSink('', imageIds, mode, new AbortController().signal)` (facade.ts:214). The controller is not retained, so dispose()/release (which aborts machine inflight attempts, machine.ts:593-603) cannot cancel this send — a session teardown (hub.ts:111-118) leaves the Host admission running to completion; only the local commitSend/notice is suppressed by the `this.disposed` check. The machine JSDoc states the intended discipline ('constructs one AbortController per SubmitAttempt at enter time and aborts it itself on release'), and this plane skips it. It also keeps a second submit-plane flag (`imageSendInFlight`) that the machine's phase does not reflect, so guardOf reports 'plain' during the flight.
findings.suggested_fix: Route the image-only send through the machine attempt plane (mint an attempt so release aborts it and dead() guards settlement), or at minimum retain the controller on the shell and abort it in dispose(). Add a case to packages/client/ui-conversation/tests/input-reference-submit.client.spec.ts: dispose during an in-flight image-only send and assert the sink signal aborts.
findings.title: Image-only submit plane bypasses the machine attempt lifecycle: untracked AbortController, dispose cannot cancel the in-flight Host send

findings.detail: MessageEditAction subscribes each armed row to the whole session snapshot with `snapshot.nodes.findLast(node => node.kind === 'user')?.seq === seq` (MessageEditAction.tsx:21). The selector returns a boolean so React does not re-render, but the selector itself runs on every snapshot emission for every mounted user-message row: with k user messages and n finalized nodes that is O(k*n) scans per streaming event, all recomputing the same single 'latest user seq' value. The chat builder already maintains per-node projections where this could be derived once.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the latest user seq once per snapshot (memoize on `snapshot.nodes` identity in a shared hook, or project it in the chat snapshot builder's legacy slice) and have the per-row selector compare against that scalar.
findings.title: MessageEditAction scans the full node list per row on every session snapshot emission

findings.detail: ChatView's turn status renders `Deep diving...` as a literal (ChatView.tsx:144, aria-live role="status"), and ToolRow renders the inspect pill as `Inspect` (ToolRow.tsx:300) — while every neighboring string in both components goes through `t()`, and ui-conversation/ui-tool both ship zh+en dictionaries. ui-plan deliberately documents its English choices ('Plan' wordmark, error-surface policy — PlanModeControl.tsx:61-68); these two carry no such comment and are ordinary UI copy, so a zh-locale user gets mixed-language chrome. The existing tests pin the English output (chat-view.client.spec.tsx:924,1018), locking the gap in.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `chat.turnStatus` / `row.inspect` keys to the conversation dictionaries (ui-conversation/src/client/locales.ts owns both namespaces — ui-tool already uses TranslateNS<'conversation'>) and route both literals through t(); update the two pinning tests.
findings.title: Hardcoded English copy bypasses the locale dictionaries: 'Deep diving...' (ChatView) and 'Inspect' (ToolRow)

findings.detail: SessionInputShell.lexicon resolves the trigger controller at subscribe time only: `subscribe: fn => this.deps.inputTriggers?.()?.lexicon.subscribe(fn) ?? (() => {})` (facade.ts:304-307). The slash/popup deps were deliberately made thunks because 'the shell is created inside the sessions provide materialization ... where slash.sessionOf cannot resolve yet' (facade.ts:27-32) — but a subscribe that lands while the controller is still absent returns a permanent noop and never re-subscribes when the controller materializes, leaving a mounted composer with an empty decoration lexicon for the session's life. The JSDoc documents the no-pipeline case but not this materialization race.
findings.suggested_fix: Make lexicon a live facade: keep a listener Set on the shell and re-bind to the controller's lexicon whenever deps.inputTriggers() first resolves (e.g. on the next track()/arbitrate() call), or document and assert the ordering guarantee that composer mounts never precede controller materialization.
findings.title: Shell lexicon observable permanently no-ops if subscribed before the input-trigger controller materializes

findings.detail: The audit priorities ask for state-machine coverage gaps: two remain. (1) Nothing exercises dispose() during an in-flight image-only send — the exact path finding 4 shows cannot be cancelled; tests/input-reference-submit.client.spec.ts covers image-only success/rejection but not teardown. (2) The facade's consumeToken/insertText splice path and the machine's `consume-token`/`insert-ref` event paths are tested separately (input-scenarios.client.spec.tsx:129 vs input-machine.client.spec.ts:394) with no parity case, so the duplication drift described above is invisible to the suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend tests/input-reference-submit.client.spec.ts with a dispose-mid-flight case asserting the sink AbortSignal fires and no settle reaches the machine; add a parity block to input-machine.client.spec.ts asserting the shell's slash/input-consume-token listener and the machine's `consume-token` event produce identical draft, occurrences, undo-log, and paste states — or delete the machine event per the dead-code finding above.
findings.title: No test pins dispose-during-send behavior of the image-only plane, nor facade/machine consume-token parity

findings.detail: carryDraft (apply.ts:253-268) moves `snapshot.draft` (the display string containing `@label` reference markers) and image ids to the next session, but not `snapshot.occurrences`, so carried reference chips demote to plain `@label` text in the new composer and will not be serialized to their model form on send — the silent downgrade the sink path otherwise refuses ('never a silent downgrade to the clipboard text', facade.ts sinkSerialized JSDoc). If chip-carrying is intentionally out of scope, the source shell is still left with draft text whose markers no longer match any table entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Either carry the occurrence table too (rebase offsets to 0 on the target shell via a dedicated verb), or carry the clipboard projection from projectClipboard instead of the display draft so the new session holds honest plain text.
findings.title: carryDraft moves reference chips as plain display text while dropping their occurrence identity

audits.summary: The chat-surface packages are in strong shape: the pure InputMachine, the ChatSnapshotBuilder's incremental folding (store/location index/legacy slice/reference-label projector), and the tool-node dispatch folding are carefully built, well JSDoc'd, and heavily tested (conversation-node-definitions covers streaming, prepend replay, interruption synthesis, and recall association). CSS modules consistently use `--rlw-*` theme tokens; the only raw-color literals (InputBar beam gradients, ContextMeter violet) are documented design exceptions. The real debt concentrates in the input wiring: two machine events (`consume-token`, `set-invalid`) have no production dispatch site — the facade re-implements consume/insert splices over setDraft and the invalid-chip feature is entirely unreachable — plus an image-only submit plane that bypasses the machine's abort lifecycle, and a ComposerBlockRegistry teardown verb that nothing ever calls. Remaining items are a hot-path selector scan in ui-message-edit and hardcoded English strings that bypass the locale dictionaries.

backlog.detail: ctx.on('agent/turn-stopping') in hooks-claude-code (src/index.ts:269-277, TODO(stop-loop-guard)) steers a continuation whenever the merged Stop-hook outcome is deny, with no counter. A deny-looping or misconfigured hook (the whole point is running untrusted scripts) makes the machine run model steps forever, each iteration spending a provider request. hooks-codex/src/index.ts:254 has the same gap. Fix: cap consecutive hook-forced continuations per turn via a Config field (convert to a normal stop with a model-visible notice when exhausted), mirror in codex, add a deny-loop-terminates test to packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/tests/.
backlog.title: Stop hooks force unbounded model continuations with no loop guard

backlog.detail: HarnessSdkJsonRpcServer.sessions is only cleared on performShutdown (packages/sdk/server/src/server.ts:59, 203-235); the protocol has no session/close. Both SDK clients mint a fresh uuid per run() when no sessionId is given (packages/sdk/client/src/api.ts:89, python/sdk/src/relay_harness/api.py:135), so a long-lived harness accumulates one live agent + session (persistence handles, session log) per call. Fix: add session/close to HarnessSdkRequestMap and dispose server-side; short term add idle TTL/LRU eviction for SDK-created agents and have run() reuse or explicitly close its session; update both SDKs' expected-output snapshots in the same PR.
backlog.title: SDK runtime sessions are never reclaimed: every run() leaks one agent until shutdown

backlog.detail: FrameQueue.push (packages/host/apiproxy/src/frame-queue.ts:13-27) has no cap and no slow-consumer policy; api-proxy.ts:620-624 pushes every session/event (high-frequency assistant deltas included) to every mux subscriber, and sseResponse enqueue never reads desiredSize. One connected-but-stalled SSE consumer (TCP zero window) grows its buffer without bound; dead queues are never removed from muxQueues; drain uses buffer.shift() (O(n^2) on large buffers). The recent 'bound sdk queues' commit covered the SDK direction — this is the last unbounded host->browser queue. Fix: cap frames or bytes, end() the subscriber on overflow (client already has reconnect + baseline replay), switch drain to a head pointer, document the bound in README/Config.
backlog.title: FrameQueue buffers per SSE subscriber are fully unbounded; a stalled consumer can exhaust host memory

backlog.detail: connection/src/client/index.ts:9 statically imports ./fixture.ts (3,335 lines of mock transcripts plus rlh-llm/rlh-session folding helpers), gated only by a runtime '?fixture' query-param check (index.ts:88-91), so no bundler can drop it from the production web bundle. Flagged identically by two independent slices. Fix: dynamic `await import('./fixture.ts')` inside the async plugin apply (or a lazy subpath export), or route it behind the __RLH_BOOT_GATE__ dev seam so tsdown tree-shakes it out.
backlog.title: 3,335-line dev FixtureApiClient (~150KB) is statically imported into the production browser bundle

backlog.detail: ui-agent-preset/src/client/settings-store.ts:38-49 calls api.settings.update({ns, patch:{default:id}}) with no expectedRevision, while the wire field exists (packages/host/apiproxy/src/api/settings.schema.ts:48-52) and every sibling writer fences on it (ui-settings settings-scope.ts:124-151, ui-permission-presets settings-store.ts:142-152, ui-settings-models editors). Two concurrent writers can silently last-write-win the default preset; the response view is also dropped instead of folded via describeFace.acceptView, leaving the mirror stale until the next push. Fix: read the namespace revision from the shared mirror, pass expectedRevision, fold the returned view back so conflicts surface as retriable errors.
backlog.title: Agent-preset default write bypasses the settings revision fencing every sibling writer uses

backlog.detail: LocalJobRegistry.store (packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts:102) removes records only in disposeOwned/disposeAll; terminal records owned by a long-lived agent stay forever, and jobs started with owner undefined (JobStart.owner optional, packages/jobs/jobs/src/types.ts:62) have no deletion path at all. list() (line 192, the model-facing surface) keeps returning every historical snapshot, inflating model-visible output indefinitely. Fix: prune terminal-and-reported records (finishedAt + grace sweep, bounded completed-cap per owner); add jobs-retention.spec.ts covering unowned/owned removal and loud failure on output of a pruned id.
backlog.title: jobs-local never prunes terminal job records; unowned jobs leak for the process lifetime and inflate the model-facing list

backlog.detail: Every searchSessions/searchEvents runs _reconcile -> _observeStable, which for every live session calls observeLive -> observeSession (src/index.ts:535, 856-870): structuredClone of header + all events, full JSON.stringify, sha256 — nothing cached, so even a fully unchanged corpus pays O(total live log bytes) per keystroke-driven search; the clone is pure waste (input already immutable). Fix: derive the fingerprint from cheap change markers (seq + header + mutation counter) or cache by (sessionId, seq, header); drop the structuredClone. Pin the behavior first with the reconciliation spec (R8): first search after a backend swap reconciles everything, second search over an unchanged corpus performs zero inspect() calls.
backlog.title: SQLite session-query re-fingerprints every live session's entire log on every search

backlog.detail: python/sdk/src/relay_harness/client.py:118-141 checks `if self._proc is not None` and assigns `self._proc = subprocess.Popen(...)` both outside self._lock; two concurrent start() calls (or concurrent RelayHarness.run) each spawn a runtime, one handle is overwritten, and the orphan's reader/stderr threads keep reading until the process exits. TS is safe by event-loop single-threading — Python-only race. Fix: move the check + Popen + thread startup inside the lock with a re-check; add a concurrent-start-spawns-one-runtime test to python/sdk/tests/test_client.py.
backlog.title: Python HarnessClient.start() double-spawn race: check and Popen are both outside the lock

backlog.detail: The authoritative window.shell preload API is re-declared as partial local interfaces in 10 client packages (ui-settings-general, ui-settings-remote — two disjoint DesktopShell sets, ui-surfaces, ui-product-shell, ui-preview, ui-files, ui-user-terminal, ui-diff, ui-git), each with its own null-safe accessor. Any preload rename or signature change silently desyncs every copy; there is no single place stating what window.shell is. Fix: one canonical DesktopShellBridge contract + desktopShell() accessor in rlh-client-runtime (React-free), each package narrowing via Pick<...>, Electron preload satisfying the interface so drift becomes a compile error.
backlog.title: Electron window.shell bridge hand-declared 11 times across 10 client packages

backlog.detail: tsconfig.host.json includes each apps/web/tests file individually while apps/web/tsconfig.json excludes the same files one-by-one from its tests glob, and scripts/run-web-snapshots.ts keeps a third serial-owners list — no gate syncs them. A new web e2e test added to the vitest.web glob but not both lists either lands in the wrong compiler face (client tsc for host-plane Context merges) or escapes typecheck entirely; drift already exists (chat-scroll-fixture.ts listed twice in both configs). Fix: a scripts gate asserting the exclude list is exactly the complement of the include list over apps/web/tests/**, or derive both from a single manifest.
backlog.title: apps/web test files are gated by three hand-maintained lists; new tests land in the wrong compile face or escape typecheck

backlog.detail: The packages/*/* fallback workspace declares entry [tests/**/*.spec.ts] and project [src/**/*.ts, tests/**/*.ts] (knip.json:246-254); .tsx globs exist only in ~30 explicit overrides. Verified missing: ui-user-questions, ui-session-tree, ui-titlebar, ui-git, ui-agents-panel, ui-surfaces, ui-files, ui-diff, ui-preview, ui-theme, ui-attachment, ui-reference, ui-brand-official, ui-memory-center, ui-sidebar — their .tsx source and .e2e/.snapshot tests are invisible to unused-file/export/dependency detection, and new client packages inherit the hole silently. Fix: widen the fallback to *.tsx/*.e2e.ts/*.snapshot.ts and delete the now-redundant overrides; knip --treat-config-hints-as-errors keeps it fails-loud.
backlog.title: knip fallback workspace config lacks .tsx/e2e/snapshot globs — 15+ client packages' tsx source escapes all knip checks

backlog.detail: agent.ts:377-383 returns false directly when phase.step===0 and the pre-step waterfall rewrites the decision to {kind:'enter', messages:[]}, skipping the tail logic every other exit runs (agent.ts:437-442 hasPending re-check + continuation). Inbox.claim('next-turn') consumes only one next-turn message, and live-driver wakes set no wakeRequested latch, so send('a'); send('b') with an empty-enter listener completes turn 1 and leaves 'b' in the inbox with no driver and no wakeup — silent shelve until the next external wakeup. The sibling `turnEnds && messages.length===0` break path behaves asymmetrically. Fix: route the empty-enter exit through the same tail (set turnEnds, break, or re-check hasPending before returning); the paired regression test in contract-regressions.spec.ts (two followups + empty enter, second message starts its own turn) is the R8 backfill.
backlog.title: Empty enter decision permanently shelves queued inbox input (skips the hasPending re-check all other turn exits run)

backlog.detail: apps/desktop/src/main/config.js:180-186 readJson catches every parse/read failure and returns fallback with no naming comment and no log; the next saveConfig persists those defaults, permanently destroying workspace/theme/restart settings — same for credentials.json (apiKey/githubToken). Violates 'misconfiguration fails loud'. Fix: on parse failure of an existing file, log via rlh.log/dialog and quarantine (config.json.corrupt-<ts>) instead of silently regenerating; at minimum name the swallow.
backlog.title: Corrupt config.json/credentials.json silently resets to defaults and the loss is then persisted

backlog.detail: A crash between writeFile(lockPath) and the finally rm (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:112-129) leaves <file>.lock; every later writer retries 2s and throws 'timed out waiting for the writer lock' forever. LocalCredentialProvider's every credential write goes through this (packages/credentials/credentials-local/src/index.ts:394); the lock contains the owner pid but isLockContention never reads it. Fix: on contention, read the pid and self-heal when process.kill(pid,0) reports it dead (same host), keep failing loud for foreign-host/unreadable locks; add a stale-lock recovery test in packages/util/atomic-write/tests.
backlog.title: Orphaned atomic-write .lock permanently bricks credential/settings writes until manual deletion

backlog.detail: TS performClose returns early when child===undefined without failSubscriptions (client.ts:418-420), and subscribe() only born-fails if closeTask/exitCode/spawnError already exist — so subscribe-then-close-then-next() never resolves. Python mirrors it (client.py:143-146 early-return before _fail_waiters), so NotificationSubscription.next() polls forever. Contract says subscriptions reject immediately after close. Fix: fail subscriptions unconditionally at the top of both close paths; add close-without-start cases to sdk-client.spec.ts and test_client.py.
backlog.title: Subscriptions created before start() hang forever after close() (TS pending forever, Python 50ms polling loop)

backlog.detail: The Python client is declared a design twin of the TS client but four behaviors have drifted: (1) initialize — TS throws SdkProtocolError on missing/malformed serverInfo (client.ts:295-302), Python's pydantic model accepts None fields (models.py:26-32); (2) malformed session.event — TS validates and throws (api.ts:155-167), Python silently skips (api.py:162-172), returning final_response='' as success; (3) RunResult — Python exposes finish_reason and validates turn/end, TS has neither and reads only data.message.content where Python falls back to data.content; (4) close semantics — TS close is terminal, Python allows restart, and teardown grace differs 6x (TS 6s EOF quiesce vs Python 1s). Fix: pick a direction per item (recommended: Python matches TS validation; TS adds finishReason + content fallback), unify the two snapshot field sets, and back each with mirrored tests (test_client.py lacks concurrent-start, subscribe-before-start, and malformed-initialize cases TS already has).
backlog.title: SDK design-twin drift bundle: initialize validation, malformed-event error propagation, RunResult projection, and close/restart semantics all differ between TS and Python

backlog.detail: WebApiClient.readWebSocket (packages/client/connection/src/client/web-api-client.ts:45-101) is the browser's only wire parser — JSON-parses every frame against serverRequestSchema, drops malformed frames with console.error and continues, drains a wake-based inbox, arms abort during CONNECTING/OPEN, closes in finally — and none of it is under test (connection/tests only has host-side specs). The malformed-frame drop-and-continue path and the pre-connect abort arm are exactly the wire-boundary behaviors AGENTS.md says to prove. Fix: add web-api-client.client.spec.ts with a stubbed global WebSocket covering malformed JSON survives, schema-invalid frame dropped while the next valid frame yields, abort during CONNECTING and during OPEN, and close-before-open.
backlog.title: No test covers the client WebSocket frame pump (WebApiClient.readWebSocket) — the browser's only wire parser

synthesis.health_summary: Round-1 audit of relay-harness (11 slices) found a codebase with unusually strong fundamentals — transactional lifecycle, revision-fenced stores, bounded queues in the SDK layer, and dense CI gating — but three dominant themes. (1) Unbounded retention/lifecycle leaks are the single biggest defect class: the host FrameQueue per SSE subscriber, SDK runtime sessions that leak one agent per run(), jobs-local terminal records (and unowned jobs with no deletion path at all), ACP sessions held for the connection lifetime, client-side session event windows, and desktop relay pending-request entries all grow without bound in long-lived processes. (2) Contract duplication and enforcement asymmetry: the Electron window.shell bridge is hand-declared 11 times, the TS/Python SDK "design twins" have drifted on validation, projection, and close semantics, the agent-preset writer alone skips settings revision fencing, and core's contained-emit pattern is copied six ways. (3) Hot-path O(n) rescans and gate holes: SQLite session-query re-fingerprints the whole corpus per search, memory-center rescans all session logs per list/read, currentAgentPreset rescans the event log each step, while knip misses all .tsx in 15+ client packages and apps/web test files sit behind three unsynced hand-maintained lists that let new tests escape typecheck. Near-misses that did not make the top 25 but are worth tracking: CircuitBreaker half-open accounting, subprocess spill-file cleanup, persistence dispose-drain deadline, JSONL zstd unbounded decompression, the Lyra-aligned frontend gaps (Files-panel syntax highlighting, render-the-app probe suite), and packages/client README missing 20 packages.
